Once upon a time there was a star called Comet. The star was very big and made of white twinkly dust. Every night, Comet's twinkles lit up the sky.

One night, something disturbing happened. Comet's twinkles began to dim and it started making strange noises. Soon all of the star's twinkles vanished and it was so quiet.

The people of Earth were worried about Comet. They thought it might have problems. They decided to send a brave astronaut to investigate.

The astronaut travelled up to the star and found out what was wrong. Comet had run out of twinkles and was too tired to shine. The astronaut gave Comet a big hug and soon it was twinkling brighter than ever before! The astronaut showed Comet how to twinkle in a special white pattern that made the night sky look extra special.

Ever since then, Comet has been twinkling in the night sky and bringing joy to all the people of Earth.

"Hello, who are you?" asked Tom. Jerry was scared, but he said, "I am Jerry, the little mouse. I was just looking for some food." Tom thought for a moment and then said, "Well, I have some food in my house. Let's be friends and share it."

From that day on, Tom and Jerry became best friends. They played together, ate together, and had lots of fun. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old cat. The cat lived by the sea. One day, the cat found a big bag of salt. The cat did not know what to do with the salt.

A little mouse saw the cat with the salt. The mouse said, "I know what to do with the salt." The cat did not want to listen to the mouse. The cat and the mouse began to fight over the salt.

The wise old cat stopped fighting and said, "Let's not fight. What do you suggest we do with the salt?" The mouse said, "We can put the salt on our food. It will taste better." The cat and the mouse became friends and shared the salt. They both learned that working together is better than fighting.

The nosy cart then made its way into the store. It quietly grabbed some apples, oranges, and bananas and put them into its cart. Then it started to hurry away.

But the grocer had seen the nosy cart! He started to chase it. He was able to catch up with it and bring it back to the store.

After that, the nosy cart was only able to get supplies when the grocery store was open and the grocer was watching. It learned its lesson: don't be too nosy!

Grandma smiled and suggested they have a tea party with muffins and hot chocolate. Lily was very happy and they sat down to enjoy their treats. 

"This muffin is yummy!" Lily said with a mouthful of crumbs. "I'm glad you like it," Grandma replied. "Maybe next time we can bake some together." 

Lily was thrilled with the idea and couldn't wait to come back to Grandma's house to bake muffins together. From that day on, they had a tea party with muffins every time Lily visited her grandma's ancient house.

Lily tried to zip up her jacket, but it was too hard. She got frustrated and said, "I can't do it, Mommy. It's too hard." Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. You can do it. Just keep trying."

Lily tried and tried, and finally, she was able to zip up her jacket all by herself! She was so happy and proud. But then, a fierce wind blew and unzipped her jacket. Lily was sad, but her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. You learned how to zip up your jacket, and that's what's important." And Lily smiled, knowing that she had accomplished something new.

Sara and Ben were bored. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked out the window and saw a big billboard. It had a picture of a dog and some words.

"What does it say?" Sara asked.

Ben tried to read the words. He knew some letters, but not all. He said, "It says... L-O-S-T. Lost. D-O-G. Dog. R-E-W-A-R-D. Reward. C-A-L-L. Call. And a number."

"What does that mean?" Sara asked.

Ben thought for a moment. He said, "It means someone lost their dog and they want to find it. They will give money to the person who finds it. They want people to call them if they see the dog."

Sara felt sad for the person who lost their dog. She said, "I wish we could help them. I love dogs."

Ben had an idea. He said, "Maybe we can. Let's search for the dog. Maybe it is hiding somewhere near our house. We can take our umbrellas and look around."

Sara liked the idea. She said, "OK, let's go. But we have to be careful. And we have to tell mom where we are going."

They put on their coats and boots and grabbed their umbrellas. They told their mom they were going to search for the lost dog. Their mom said, "Be careful and don't go too far. And come back soon."

Sara and Ben nodded and went outside. They looked under cars, behind bushes, in trash cans, and in alleys. They did not see the dog. They saw other things, like a cat, a bird, a rat, and a can. But no dog.

They were about to give up when they saw something mysterious. It was a big box with a hole in it. It was behind a fence. They heard a noise from inside the box. It sounded like a bark.

They ran to the fence and looked through the hole. They saw the dog from the billboard. It was brown and white and had a red collar. It looked scared and wet.

Sara and Ben were happy. They said, "We found you! We found you!"

They tried to open the fence, but it was locked. They said, "Don't worry, we will help you. We will call the number on the billboard. They will come and get you."

They took out their mom's phone and dialed the number. A voice answered. It said, "Hello?"

Sara said, "Hello, we found your dog. It is in a box behind a fence. We are near the billboard. Can you come and get it?"

The voice said, "Oh, thank you, thank you. You are very kind. I will be there in a minute. What are your names?"

Sara said, "I am Sara and this is Ben. We like dogs."

The voice said, "I am Tom. I am the owner of the dog. His name is Spot. He ran away from me yesterday. I was very worried. You are very brave and smart to search for him. I will give you a reward."

Sara and Ben said, "You're welcome. We are happy to help. We don't need a reward. We just want Spot to be safe and happy."

They waited for Tom to arrive. They talked to Spot through the hole. They told him jokes and stories. They made him feel better.

Soon, they saw a car stop near the billboard. A man got out. He had a key and a leash. He opened the fence and took out the box. He opened the box and hugged Spot. He said, "Spot, I missed you so much. You are my best friend. Thank you, Sara and Ben, for finding him. You are my heroes."

He gave them each a hug and a kiss. He gave them a card with his name and number. He said, "If you ever want to visit Spot, you can call me. He would love to see you again. And I would love to see you too. You are very nice kids."

Sara and Ben said, "Thank you, Tom. We would love to visit Spot. He is very cute and funny. We are glad you are together again."

They waved goodbye to Tom and Spot. They went back to their house. They told their mom what happened. Their mom was proud of them. She said, "You did a good thing today. You helped someone in need. You made a new friend. You are very good kids."

Sara and Ben smiled. They said, "We had fun. We learned a new word. We searched for a dog. We solved a mystery. We are very happy kids."

Sam did not like soup. He thought soup was dull and wet and made his mouth hot. He wanted to eat bread and cheese and grapes for lunch, like his big sister Lily. But Mom said he had to eat soup, because soup was good for him and would make him strong and healthy.

"No soup!" Sam said, pushing his bowl away. "Soup is yuck!"

"Sam, you have to eat your soup," Mom said, trying to be patient. "It has carrots and potatoes and chicken in it. You like those things, don't you?"

Sam shook his head. He did not care what was in the soup. He only saw the dull brown liquid that smelled like nothing. He crossed his arms and pouted.

"Please, Sam, just try a little bit," Mom said, holding a spoonful of soup to his mouth. "It's not hot, I promise. It's just warm and tasty."

Sam turned his head away. He did not want to try the soup. He insisted on eating something else. He said, "No, no, no!"

Mom sighed. She did not know what to do with Sam. She loved him very much, but he was being very stubborn. She looked at Lily, who was eating her soup quietly and politely. She wished Sam would be more like Lily.

Lily saw Mom's sad face. She felt sorry for Mom and Sam. She had an idea. She said to Sam, "Sam, do you want to play a game with me?"

Sam liked games. He looked at Lily with curiosity. He said, "What game?"

Lily smiled. She said, "It's called the soup game. We pretend that the soup is something else, like a magic potion or a treasure or a dinosaur. And we make up stories about it and eat it. It's fun!"

Sam thought about it. He liked magic potions and treasures and dinosaurs. He liked stories and fun. He said, "Okay, I'll play the soup game."

Lily clapped her hands. She said, "Great! Let's start. I'll go first. This soup is a magic potion that can make us fly. If we drink it, we can soar in the sky and see the clouds and the birds and the sun. Do you want to try?"

Sam nodded. He said, "Yes, I want to fly." He took a sip of the soup. It was not so dull and wet and hot after all. It was warm and tasty and made him feel happy. He said, "Mmm, this is good!"

Mom smiled. She was glad that Lily helped Sam to eat his soup. She said, "Well done, Lily and Sam. You are both very clever and creative. And you are both eating your soup, which is good for you. I'm proud of you."

Lily and Sam smiled back. They said, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. And we love soup!" They finished their bowls and asked for more. They played the soup game until they were full and satisfied. They had fun and learned to like something new. They were happy.

Tom and Sue say yes, they are hungry. They drive to the diner and sit at a table. Mom orders a burger and fries for herself, and chicken nuggets and apple juice for Tom and Sue.

The food comes and they start to eat. Tom takes a bite of his chicken nugget and makes a funny face. He says, "Mom, this is spicy! It hurts my mouth!"

Mom says, "Oh, I'm sorry, Tom. I think they put some sauce on your nuggets. Do you want to trade with me? My burger is not spicy."

Tom says yes, he wants to trade. He gives his nuggets to Mom and takes her burger. He takes a bite and says, "This is better. Thank you, Mom."

Sue says, "I like my nuggets. They are not spicy. They are yummy."

Mom says, "I'm glad you like them, Sue. You are a brave girl. You can try new things."

They finish their lunch and pay the bill. They drive home and read their books. They have a good day.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a pond with many frogs. They wanted to catch a frog and make it their friend.

They ran to the pond and looked for a frog. They saw a big green frog sitting on a rock. They tried to grab it, but it jumped away. They saw a small brown frog hiding under a leaf. They tried to touch it, but it hopped away. They saw a yellow frog with spots on its back. They tried to hold it, but it slipped away.

They were sad and tired. They could not catch any frog. They sat on the grass and rested. They heard a croak. They looked up and saw a frog on a branch. It was blue and shiny. It looked at them and smiled.

"Hello, little ones," the frog said. "Why are you sad?"

"We want to catch a frog and make it our friend," Lily said. "But all the frogs run away from us."

The frog nodded. "I understand. Frogs are shy and scared of big people. They like to be free and safe. But I am not like other frogs. I am a magic frog. I can talk and change colors. And I like to make new friends."

"Wow, you are a magic frog!" Tom said. "Can we be your friends?"

"Of course, you can," the frog said. "But you have to be gentle and kind. And you have to let me go when I want to. Can you do that?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They promised to be gentle and kind. And they promised to let the frog go when he wanted to. The frog jumped down from the branch and landed on Lily's hand. He felt soft and warm. He gave her a sweet kiss on the cheek. Lily giggled.

The frog jumped to Tom's hand. He felt smooth and cool. He gave him a sweet kiss on the nose. Tom laughed.

They played with the frog for a while. They asked him questions and he told them stories. They learned his name was Bluey. They told him their names and he repeated them. They had fun and forgot their sadness.

They thanked Bluey for being their friend. They said goodbye and let him go. He jumped back to the branch and waved at them. He changed his color to match the sky. He croaked and smiled.

Lily and Tom smiled back. They felt happy and lucky. They had met a magic frog. They had made a sweet friend. They ran back to their mom and dad and told them everything. They never forgot Bluey. And Bluey never forgot them.

Spot had an idea. He found a big, red ball and showed it to Whiskers. Whiskers saw the ball and became excited. He jumped up and started to play with Spot. They played all day and had lots of fun. From that day on, Whiskers was not lazy anymore, and they were the best neighbors.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a helpful ice cream man named Tom. Tom loved to give ice cream to all the kids in the town. One hot day, Tom was driving his ice cream truck when he saw a little girl named Sue. Sue looked sad. Tom wanted to help her feel better, so he stopped the truck and asked, "Why are you sad, Sue?"

Sue said, "I lost my stuff. My mom will be mad." Tom thought for a moment and had an idea. "Let's look for your stuff together," he said. As they walked around, Tom gave Sue a big ice cream cone to make her feel better.

They looked and looked, but they could not find Sue's stuff. Sue's ice cream started to melt in the hot sun. Just as the ice cream was about to fall off the cone, they found Sue's stuff under a tree. Sue was so happy, and she thanked Tom for being so helpful. They both laughed as Sue's melted ice cream dripped onto her stuff. The day was saved, and Sue learned that helpful friends can make any day better.

The man said, "There's a fire in the forest. The trees are burning and the mist is coming from the smoke." Timmy was sad to hear that the trees were burning, but he was happy that the man was organized and had a plan to put out the fire.

Sally said, "Let's help the man organize and put out the fire!" Timmy and Sally ran to get some water and helped put out the fire. They were happy that they could help save the trees.

As they were decorating, Lily noticed a bee buzzing around the poppies. She asked her mommy if the bee was going to hurt the flowers. Her mommy said no, but Lily was still scared. Later that night, Lily heard a loud buzzing sound and saw the bee had come back. She tried to shoo it away, but accidentally knocked over the vase of poppies.

Lily was sad because she had ruined the pretty flowers. Her mommy hugged her and said it was okay, they could buy more. But Lily knew she had learned a lesson to be careful when decorating with fragile things. From then on, she made sure to be extra careful when decorating with her favorite flower, the poppy.

But the cows didn't listen. They kept playing around. Jack didn't know what to do. He went to ask his friend, the horse, for advice. "Horse, my cows are not behaving. What should I do?" he asked. The horse replied, "Maybe you can try giving them a treat after they finish their food. That might make them behave better." 

Jack followed the horse's advice and gave the cows a treat after they ate their food. The cows were happy and started behaving. Jack was happy too. He learned that sometimes, being stubborn doesn't help and it's better to ask for help.

One day, their mom came to their room and said, "Lily and Ben, you have to organize your toys. You cannot play with them if they are all over the place. It is not safe and not nice. You have to put them in the boxes and on the shelves. Then you can find them easily and have more space to play."

You can play a game and see who can organize faster and better. You can be cheerful and sing a song while you organize. You will see how much better your room will look and feel when you are done."

Lily was curious. She wanted to see the barber. She asked her mom if they could go inside. Her mom said, "Okay, but we have to be quiet and polite. The barber is busy working."

They went inside the shop. Lily saw a man with a white coat and a white hat. He had scissors and a comb in his hands. He was cutting a boy's hair. The boy looked happy. Lily thought the man was the barber.

She walked up to him and said, "Hello, Mr. Barber. Can you cut my doll's hair too? She has long hair and I want to make her look like a princess."

The man smiled and said, "Hello, little girl. I'm sorry, but I can't cut your doll's hair. I only cut real hair. But you can lend me your doll for a minute and I can pretend to cut her hair. Would you like that?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. Thank you, Mr. Barber. You are very nice." She gave him her doll and watched him pretend to cut her hair. He made funny noises and said, "Snip, snip, snip. There, your doll looks like a princess now. She has a beautiful hairstyle."

Lily was happy. She took her doll back and said, "Thank you, Mr. Barber. You are very good at cutting hair. Can I come back and see you again?"

The man said, "You're welcome, little girl. You are very sweet. You can come back anytime. Maybe next time you can bring another doll or a friend."

Lily hugged her doll and said, "Okay, Mr. Barber. I will. Goodbye." She waved at him and left the shop with her mom. She was glad she met the barber. He was a nice man who liked to play with dolls.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park after school. One day, they saw a big jar of jelly on a bench. It was red and shiny and looked yummy.

"Let's eat some jelly!" Tom said. He ran to the bench and opened the jar.

Lily followed him, but she was not sure. "Who left the jelly here?" she asked. "Maybe it is not for us."

Tom did not care. He put his hand in the jar and grabbed some jelly. He put it in his mouth and smiled. "It is sweet and soft. Try some, Lily!"

Lily was curious. She reached for the jar, but then she saw something strange. The jelly started to glow. It was not red anymore. It was green and blue and purple. It sparkled and flashed. It made a funny noise.

Lily was scared. She dropped the jar and ran away. "Tom, Tom, come with me! The jelly is bad! It is glowing!"

Tom was surprised. He looked at the jelly and saw the colors and the light. He felt a tickle in his mouth and his stomach. He spit out the jelly and threw the jar. He ran after Lily. "Lily, Lily, wait for me! The jelly is weird! It is glowing!"

They ran to the playground and hid behind the slide. They hugged each other and breathed hard. They looked at the bench and saw the jelly still glowing. It was moving and growing. It looked like a monster.

Lily and Tom were afraid. They wanted to go home. But they did not want to pass the jelly. They did not know what to do.

Then they heard a voice. It was Mr. Lee, the park keeper. He was walking with his dog, Spot. He saw the jelly and said, "Oh, no! Someone left their science project here. This is not jelly. This is slime. It glows when you touch it. It is harmless, but messy."

He picked up the jar and the slime. He put them in his bag. He saw Lily and Tom behind the slide. He smiled and said, "Hello, kids. Are you OK? Did you see the slime?"

Lily and Tom came out of their hiding place. They nodded and said, "Yes, we saw the slime. We thought it was jelly. We ate some. It was glowing."

Mr. Lee laughed and said, "Don't worry, kids. The slime is not poisonous. It will not hurt you. It will just make you glow for a while. You are brave to try something new. But next time, be careful what you eat. You never know what you might find in the park."

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Mr. Lee. We are sorry for the mess. We will not eat strange things again. We will only eat our own food."

Mr. Lee said, "That's good, kids. Now, go home and wash your hands and your mouths. And don't forget to brush your teeth. Have a nice day!"

Lily and Tom said, "Bye, Mr. Lee. Bye, Spot. Have a nice day, too!"

They walked home, holding hands. They still glowed a little, but they did not mind. They learned a lesson and had an adventure. They were still best friends.

Just then, another boy named Jack came over and saw the gem. He said, "Hey, that's my gem! I lost it earlier today."

Lily and Tommy looked at each other, feeling confused. They didn't know what to do. Lily said, "We didn't know it was yours. We just found it on the ground."

Jack looked at the gem and said, "I'm sorry for getting upset. It's just that this gem is very special to me. It's been in my family for generations. Thank you for finding it."

Lily, Tommy, and Jack all smiled and played together in the park, happy to have resolved their conflict over the precious gem.

Once upon a time, there was a pig with an orange nose. The pig had a big problem and couldn't solve it. He was so sad! But then one day, he thought of a plan. He decided to ask the big orange cat for help.

Then, finally, the cat had a plan! He told the pig to wiggle his nose, three times really fast. The pig did as he was told, and much to his surprise, it worked! His problem was solved. The pig was so happy he could hardly stand it! He thanked the cat for helping him solve his problem. 

From then on, the pig and the cat were best friends, solving all sorts of wonderful problems together.

The light shone brightly, shimmering and twinkling like it was alive. Joe was so happy and he realised how lucky he was to see such a wonderful thing. He stood there, entranced and he felt a warmth inside him that made him beam.

He reached out to touch the light, but the moment he did, it changed colour, changing from pale to a warm and inviting orange. Joe smiled and he wondered what else the light could do. He knew he was going to admire it for a long time.

The bird saw the frog and said, "Hello little frog! Why are you here?" The frog said, "I want to escape from the pond and find a way to make my leg feel better." The bird smiled and said, "I can help you! I know where to find some special leaves that can heal your leg." The frog was so happy and thanked the bird. Together, they flew to find the special leaves and the frog's leg felt better. From that day on, the frog knew that even when things hurt, he could escape and find help.

Her mom said, "Some people say that the universe started with a big bang. That means that everything was very small and very hot and then it exploded and stretched and grew and cooled down. And it is still stretching and growing and changing."

Anna said, "That sounds scary. Does that mean that the stars will go away?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Your wand is not magic, Sara. It is just a toy. But you can help me make a real cake. Do you want to do that?"

Sara nodded. She liked to help her mom. She followed her mom to the kitchen. Her mom gave her a bowl and a spoon. She said, "We need to mix some things to make a cake. Can you help me?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can help. What do we need?"

Her mom said, "We need flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and milk. Can you say those words?"

Sara repeated the words. She said, "Flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and milk."

Her mom said, "Very good. Now, we need to measure them. Can you help me measure them?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can help. How do we measure them?"

Her mom said, "We use cups and spoons. I will show you. This is a cup. This is a spoon. We need one cup of flour. Can you pour the flour into the cup?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can pour the flour." She took the bag of flour and poured some into the cup. But she poured too much. The flour spilled over the cup and onto the table.

Her mom said, "Oops, that's too much. We need to take some out. Can you use the spoon to scoop some out?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can scoop some out." She took the spoon and scooped some flour out of the cup. But she scooped too much. The flour flew out of the spoon and onto the floor.

Her mom said, "Oh no, that's too much. We need to put some back. Can you use the spoon to put some back?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can put some back." She took the spoon and put some flour back into the cup. But she put too little. The cup was not full.

Her mom said, "Oh dear, that's too little. We need to add some more. Can you pour some more?"

Sara said, "No, I can't pour some more. I don't want to pour some more. I don't like flour. It is messy. It is not fun. I want cake."

Her mom said, "I know, Sara. I know you want cake. But we need flour to make cake. Flour is important. Flour is good. Flour will yield a yummy cake. Do you know what yield means?"

Sara said, "No, I don't know what yield means."

Her mom said, "Yield means to make or to give. When we mix flour with other things, we yield a cake. We make a cake. We give a cake. Do you understand?"

Sara said, "Yes, I understand. Yield means to make or to give. I want to yield a cake. I want to make a cake. I want to give a cake. Can we please yield a cake?"

Her mom said, "Yes, we can yield a cake. But we need to finish measuring the flour. Can you try one more time?"

Sara said, "Yes, I can try one more time. I will be careful. I will be gentle. I will be good. I will yield a cake."

She poured some more flour into the cup. She poured just enough. The cup was full. She smiled. She said, "Look, mom. I did it. I measured the flour. I yielded the flour."

Her mom said, "Yes, you did it. You measured the flour. You yielded the flour. You are a good helper. You are a good princess. I am proud of you."

She hugged Sara. She said, "Now, let's measure the other things. And then we can bake the cake. And then we can eat the cake. And then we can be happy."

Sara said, "Yes, let's do that. I love you, mom. I love cake. I love being a princess."

"I'm looking for nuts," replied Nutty.

"I see," said the lion. "Well, I'm hungry too. But I don't have any money to buy food. Do you know where I can find something to eat?"

Nutty thought for a moment and said, "There's a tree over there with very expensive nuts. Maybe we can share them?"

The lion smiled and said, "Thank you, little squirrel. You're very kind." And together, they climbed the tree and shared the expensive nuts. From that day on, Nutty and the lion became good friends and went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a cute bunny named Fluffy. Fluffy had a secret hiding place under a big rock in the forest. One day, Fluffy was playing with his friend, a little bird named Tweetie.

Tweetie asked, "Fluffy, where do you go when you disappear?"

Fluffy replied, "It's a secret. I can't tell you."

Tweetie got upset and said, "But we're friends! Friends don't keep secrets from each other."

Fluffy felt bad and realized he was wrong. He took Tweetie to his secret hiding place under the big rock and showed him around. Tweetie was so happy and said, "Wow, this is amazing! Thank you for showing me your secret place, Fluffy."

From that day on, Fluffy and Tweetie played together in their secret hiding place under the big rock. They learned that it's always better to share secrets with friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Hoppy. Hoppy loved to jump and play in the pond all day long. One day, he saw a big bird flying above him. The bird swooped down and grabbed Hoppy with his sharp claws. Hoppy was scared and tried to escape, but the bird was too strong.

The bird flew high into the sky with Hoppy in his grasp. Hoppy looked down and saw the pond getting smaller and smaller. He knew he had to do something to get away from the bird. Suddenly, he had an idea. He used his strong legs to wiggle free from the bird's grip and fell down towards the ground. Luckily, he landed safely in the pond.

Hoppy was so happy to be back in the pond, he jumped up and down with joy. His friend, a little fish named Swimmy, asked him what happened. Hoppy told him the whole story and Swimmy was amazed. "Wow, Hoppy! You are so brave and original!" Swimmy said. Hoppy blushed and smiled, feeling proud of himself. From that day on, Hoppy was always careful to watch out for big birds and never let his guard down again.

As the sun went down, they went home. Tim told his mom about his dream and the orange ball. She smiled and said, "Maybe your dream will come true one day." Tim went to bed, hoping to see the orange room in his dreams again.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to run with speed through the forest. One sunny day, Remy saw a big turtle named Toby. Toby walked slow and it was difficult for him to move fast. Remy asked Toby, "Do you want to race with me?" Toby just nod his head.

The race began and Remy ran very fast. He looked back and saw Toby was far behind. Remy thought, "I am fast. I will win for sure." So, he decided to take a nap under a tree. Toby kept walking slow and steady. He did not stop or take a nap.

When Remy woke up, he saw Toby was about to win the race. Remy tried to run fast, but it was too late. Toby won the race. Remy felt sad but learned a lesson. He knew that being slow and steady can win the race too. From that day on, Remy and Toby became good friends and always helped each other.

Anna came out of her room and saw the dragon. He was not scary. He was kind and gentle. He smiled at her and said, "Hello, princess. I am Leo. I came to unite with you. You are my mate. We belong together."

Anna was surprised. She had never seen a dragon before. But she felt something in her heart. She felt love. She smiled back and said, "Hello, Leo. I am Anna. I came to unite with you too. You are my mate. We belong together."

They hugged and kissed. They were happy. They decided to leave the castle and see the world. They had many adventures and made many friends. They were a strong and united couple. They lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were very hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. Mom and Dad said they would take them to a restaurant. Tom and Lily were happy.

They got in the car and drove to the restaurant. It was a big building with many lights and people. Tom and Lily saw a sign that said "Pizza". They liked pizza. They hoped they would get some.

They went inside the restaurant and sat at a table. A man came and gave them menus. He said he would come back soon. Tom and Lily looked at the menus. They had many pictures of food. Tom and Lily tried to read the words, but they were too hard. They asked Mom and Dad what they were.

Mom and Dad said they were different kinds of pizza. They said they could choose what they wanted on their pizza. Tom and Lily thought for a moment. They decided what they liked.

"I want cheese and ham and pineapple," Tom said.

"I want cheese and pepperoni and olives," Lily said.

Mom and Dad nodded. They told the man what they wanted. The man said he would bring their pizza soon. Tom and Lily waited.

They were very hungry. They wanted their pizza now. They looked around the restaurant. They saw other people eating their food. They smelled something good. They wondered where their pizza was.

They saw a door that said "Kitchen". They thought maybe their pizza was behind the door. They wanted to see. They got up from their chairs and walked to the door. They peeked inside.

They saw a big mess. They saw pots and pans and dishes and food everywhere. They saw a man with a big hat and a big knife. He was yelling and throwing things. He looked angry. He looked terrible.

Tom and Lily were scared. They ran back to their table. They told Mom and Dad what they saw. Mom and Dad looked surprised. They said they were sorry. They said they would find another restaurant.

They got up from their table and left the restaurant. They got in the car and drove away. They hoped they would find a better place to eat. They hoped they would get some yummy pizza. They hoped they would never see the terrible man again.

Sam was a friendly boy who liked to play with his toys and his dog. One day, he saw a big truck on the road and wanted to touch it. He ran across the street without looking. His dog barked and chased him. A car was coming fast and could not stop.

"Sam, watch out!" his mom shouted. She ran after him too. The dog reached Sam first and pushed him out of the way. The car hit the dog instead. Sam was safe, but the dog was hurt.

Sam cried and hugged his dog. His mom hugged him too. She was scared and angry. "Sam, you were very naughty. You could have been hit by the car. You have to look both ways before you cross the street. You have to listen to me. Do you understand?" she said.

Sam nodded and said sorry. He loved his mom and his dog. He did not want to make them sad. He learned his lesson. He said thank you to his dog for saving him. The dog licked his face.

They took the dog to the vet. The vet said the dog needed an operation to fix his leg. Sam was worried. He did not want his dog to be in pain. He asked the vet if he could stay with his dog. The vet was friendly and said yes. He said Sam could help him by being brave and calm. He said the operation would make the dog better.

Sam stayed with his dog and held his paw. He told his dog he loved him and he was sorry. He said he would never run across the street again. He said he would prevent any more accidents. The dog wagged his tail. The vet did the operation and said it was a success. The dog would be fine.

Sam was happy and relieved. He thanked the vet and his mom. He hugged his dog and said he was proud of him. He learned to be careful and responsible. He learned to appreciate his mom and his dog. He learned to prevent trouble and be friendly. He was a good boy.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the park with their moms. There are many things to do in the park. They see swings, slides, sand, and a big drum.

"Look, a drum!" Lily says. "I want to play with it."

"Me too!" Sam says. "Let's go and see if it is available."

They run to the drum. It is very big and shiny. It has two sticks to hit it. But there is a problem. There is another boy playing with the drum. He is making loud noises.

"Excuse me, can we play with the drum too?" Lily asks.

"No, it is mine!" the boy says. "Go away!"

Lily and Sam feel sad. They want to play with the drum, but the boy is not nice. They do not know what to do.

"Let's watch him for a while," Sam says. "Maybe he will get tired and leave."

They sit on a bench and watch the boy. He hits the drum very hard. He does not look happy. He looks angry.

After some time, the boy's mom comes. She looks at the drum and at the boy.

"Time to go, Tommy," she says. "You have played enough with the drum. It is not yours. It is for everyone to share."

The boy does not want to go. He cries and kicks. His mom picks him up and takes him away.

Lily and Sam are happy. Now the drum is available. They run to the drum and take the sticks. They hit the drum gently. They make nice sounds. They smile and laugh.

They play with the drum until their moms call them. They put the sticks back and say goodbye to the drum.

"Thank you, drum," Lily says.

They hold hands and go to their moms. They had a lot of fun in the park. They are good friends.

Sara and Ben went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. They liked to watch them and learn their names. But Sara's favorite animal was the ostrich. She liked its long neck, big eyes, and fluffy feathers.

"Mom, can I feed the ostrich?" Sara asked.

"Sure, honey. Here, take some of these seeds. But be careful, they can peck hard," mom said.

Sara took the seeds and walked to the fence. She saw a big ostrich standing near a tree. She held out her hand with the seeds and called, "Hello, ostrich. Do you want some food?"

The ostrich looked at Sara and nodded. It came closer and ate the seeds from her hand. Sara smiled and stroked its neck. She felt happy.

Ben saw Sara and the ostrich. He felt jealous. He wanted to feed the ostrich too. But he did not have any seeds. He looked around and saw a banana peel on the ground. He picked it up and ran to the fence.

"Hey, ostrich. I have something better for you. Here, try this," Ben said. He threw the banana peel over the fence.

The ostrich saw the banana peel and shook its head. It did not like it. It spat it out and ran away. It hid behind the tree and did not come out.

Sara saw what Ben did. She felt angry and sad. She said, "Ben, that was not nice. You scared the ostrich. It does not like banana peels. It likes seeds. You should not throw trash at animals. You should be kind and respectful."

Ben saw Sara's face and the ostrich's face. He felt sorry. He said, "Sara, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I wanted to feed the ostrich too, but I did not have any seeds. I thought it would like the banana peel. I did not mean to scare it. I want to change and be a better brother."

Sara hugged Ben and said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to promise me to never do that again. And you have to say sorry to the ostrich too."

Ben nodded and said, "I promise, Sara. And I'm sorry, ostrich. Please come out and be my friend."

The ostrich heard Ben's voice and peeked from behind the tree. It saw Ben's face and Sara's face. It felt curious and brave. It came out and walked to the fence. It nodded and said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you too. You can be my friend. But next time, please bring me some seeds."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, ostrich. You are very nice. Next time, I will bring you some seeds. And I will share them with Sara too."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are very nice too. And I will share them with you too."

Mom saw Sara, Ben, and the ostrich. She felt proud and happy. She said, "Well done, Sara and Ben. You learned a valuable lesson today. You learned to be kind, respectful, and forgiving. And you made a new friend. That's what makes a good family and a good world."

Sara, Ben, and the ostrich agreed. They said, "Yes, mom. We learned a lot today. And we had a lot of fun. We love you, mom. And we love each other. And we love the ostrich too."

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They ran to the tree and looked at the ground.

"Look, Lily, we have shadows!" Ben said. He pointed at the dark shapes on the grass. "My shadow is big and tall. Your shadow is small and cute."

Lily nodded. She liked her shadow. She moved her arms and legs and saw her shadow do the same. She smiled and said, "Our shadows are like us. They follow us everywhere."

Ben nodded too. He moved his head and saw his shadow do the same. He laughed and said, "Our shadows are funny. They copy us all the time."

They played with their shadows for a while. They made funny poses and shapes. They had fun.

Then they saw a man walking by. He had a hat and a coat and a bag. He looked different from them. He also had a shadow, but his shadow was not like his. His shadow was small and round and had ears and a tail.

"Look, Lily, his shadow is different!" Ben said. He pointed at the man's shadow. "His shadow is not like him. His shadow is like a dog."

Lily looked and saw the man's shadow. She was surprised and curious. She said, "Why is his shadow different? Why is his shadow like a dog?"

The man heard them and stopped. He smiled and said, "Hello, kids. I see you are playing with your shadows. Do you like them?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, we like our shadows. They are like us."

The man nodded. He said, "That's good. Your shadows are very nice. Do you want to see my shadow?"

Lily and Ben nodded again. They said, "Yes, we want to see your shadow. Why is your shadow different? Why is your shadow like a dog?"

The man laughed. He said, "My shadow is different because I have a friend with me. He is hiding behind me. He is my dog. His name is Spot. Do you want to meet him?"

Lily and Ben nodded again. They said, "Yes, we want to meet him. We like dogs."

The man moved aside and showed them his dog. He was a small and round and had ears and a tail. He was black and white and had a spot on his eye. He wagged his tail and licked their faces.

Lily and Ben giggled. They said, "Hello, Spot. You are a nice dog. You have a nice shadow."

The man smiled. He said, "Thank you, kids. You are very kind. You have nice shadows too. Do you want to play with us?"

Lily and Ben nodded again. They said, "Yes, we want to play with you. We like to play with shadows."

They played with the man and his dog. They ran and jumped and slid. They saw their shadows and Spot's shadow. They had fun. They learned that shadows can be different and that different can be good. They made new friends. They were happy.

Lily and Ben nodded. They took off their clothes and put them back in the box. They followed their mom downstairs. They were happy. They had a lot of fun in the attic, but they also liked to share and help others.

Sara remembered. She felt nervous. She had put it in the sack.

Tim and Sam are playing with their toys. They have cars, trains, blocks and animals. They like to sort their toys by color and shape. Tim has a red car, a blue train, a yellow block and a green frog. Sam has a black car, a white train, a orange block and a brown bear.

"Look, I have a scale!" Sam says. He shows Tim a toy scale that he found in the closet. It has two plates and a needle. "We can weigh our toys and see which one is heavier."

"Okay, let's try it!" Tim says. He puts his red car on one plate and his blue train on the other. The needle moves to the side of the train. "The train is heavier than the car!" he says.

"Let me try!" Sam says. He puts his black car on one plate and his white train on the other. The needle moves to the side of the car. "The car is heavier than the train!" he says.

They try with different toys and see how the needle moves. They have fun comparing their toys.

Then they see a dirty sock on the floor. It is gray and smelly. They wonder how much it weighs.

"Let's put it on the scale!" Tim says.

"No, don't do that!" Sam says. "It is dirty and yucky. It will make the scale dirty too."

But Tim does not listen. He picks up the sock and puts it on one plate. The needle moves all the way to the side of the sock. The sock is very heavy.

"Wow, the sock is heavier than all the toys!" Tim says.

But then he sees that the sock has left a stain on the plate. The plate is dirty and wet. He feels sorry.

"Oh no, I made the scale dirty!" he says.

Sam is angry. He takes the sock and throws it in the trash. He wipes the plate with a cloth. He looks at Tim.

"You should not put dirty things on the scale!" he says. "The scale is for toys, not for socks. You have to be careful and clean."

Tim is sad. He knows he made a mistake. He says sorry to Sam.

"I'm sorry, Sam. I was curious. I did not mean to make the scale dirty. Can we still be friends?" he says.

Sam thinks for a moment. He sees that Tim is sincere. He smiles and hugs him.

"It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. We can still be friends. But next time, please ask me before you do something like that. And let's sort our toys again. That was fun." he says.

They go back to their toys and sort them by color and shape. They forget about the sock and the scale. They are happy and play together.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they find a big book with many pictures of animals. They open the book and see a lot of different animals. Some have fur, some have feathers, some have scales.

"Look at this one!" Lily says, pointing to a picture of a zebra. "It has black and white stripes on its skin. How unique!"

"Yes, it is unique," Ben agrees. "Do you know what it is called?"

Lily shakes her head. "No, I don't. Do you?"

Ben smiles. "Yes, I do. I can tell you, but you have to guess first. What sound does it make?"

Lily thinks hard. She tries to remember the sounds of different animals. She makes a sound like a cow. "Moo?"

Ben laughs. "No, that's not it. A cow has spots, not stripes. Try again."

Lily makes a sound like a horse. "Neigh?"

Ben shakes his head. "No, that's not it either. A horse has a mane, not stripes. One more try."

Lily makes a sound like a cat. "Meow?"

Ben claps his hands. "No, that's wrong, but very funny. A cat has whiskers, not stripes. Do you give up?"

Lily nods. "Yes, I give up. What is it?"

Ben tells her. "It is a zebra. It makes a sound like this: Zee-zee-zee!"

Lily repeats the sound. "Zee-zee-zee! That's a funny sound. I like it. A zebra is a unique animal."

Ben nods. "Yes, it is. And you know what? You are a unique person. You have your own skin, your own voice, your own name. No one else is like you."

Lily smiles. "Thank you, Ben. You are a unique person too. You are my friend. I like you."

They hug each other. Then they turn the page and look at more animals. They have fun guessing their names and sounds. They learn a lot from the big book.

"Me too!" Ben says. "I like to spin!"

They spin and spin and spin. But then Lily feels something in her stomach. It is not a good feeling. She feels sick.

"Ben, stop!" Lily says. "I want to get off!"

But Ben does not hear her. He is having too much fun. He pushes the thing harder and it spins faster.

Lily feels worse and worse. She cannot hold it anymore. She throws up on the thing. It is messy and smelly.

Ben sees it and stops pushing. He looks at Lily and the thing. He feels bad.

"Oh, Lily, I'm sorry!" Ben says. "I did not know you were sick!"

Lily gets off the thing. She is dizzy and pale. She wipes her mouth.

"It's okay, Ben," Lily says. "You did not mean it. But I don't like to spin anymore. It makes my stomach hurt."

Ben gets off the thing too. He hugs Lily and says sorry again.

"Let's go to the bench and rest," Ben says. "Maybe we can have some water and a snack."

Lily nods. She is glad Ben is her friend. They walk to the bench and sit down. They do not spin anymore. They feel better.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a squirrel on a tree. The squirrel had a big nut in its mouth.

"Look, a squirrel!" Lily said. "It is eating a nut."

"Can we have a nut too?" Ben asked. He was hungry.

Lily and Ben ran to the tree. They tried to reach the squirrel. But the squirrel was too fast. It ran away to another tree.

"Come back, squirrel!" Ben shouted. "Share your nut with us!"

The squirrel did not listen. It found a hole in the tree. It hid its nut in the hole.

Lily and Ben were sad. They wanted a nut. They looked around. They saw some nuts on the ground. They picked them up.

"Maybe these nuts are good," Lily said. She cracked one open. She took a bite.

"Yuck!" Lily spat. "This nut is bitter. It tastes bad."

Ben tried his nut too. He made a face. He did not like it.

"These nuts are not good," Ben said. "They are not like the squirrel's nut."

Lily and Ben threw the nuts away. They learned a lesson. They learned that not all nuts are the same. They learned that the squirrel knew which nuts were good and which nuts were bad. They learned that the squirrel was smart.

They decided to leave the squirrel alone. They went to find something else to play with. They hoped to find something sweet.

Tim and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big tree. They want to climb the tree.

"Can we climb the tree?" Tim asks Sue.

"Yes, let's climb the tree!" Sue says.

They run to the tree. They hold the branches. They pull themselves up. They go higher and higher. They feel happy.

They reach the top of the tree. They look around. They see the sky, the birds, the flowers, the swings. They see a big pile of trash. It is smelly.

"Yuck, what is that?" Tim says.

"That is trash. It is old and dirty. It makes the air smelly." Sue says.

"Who put the trash there?" Tim says.

"I don't know. Maybe some bad people. They don't care about the park." Sue says.

"That is not nice. They should clean the trash. The park is for everyone. The park is for us." Tim says.

"Yes, you are right. The park is for us. We love the park. We should take care of the park." Sue says.

They nod. They smile. They hug. They climb down the tree. They go to the swings. They have fun. They are good friends. They are good to the park.

Lily liked to design things. She used paper, crayons, scissors and glue to make cards, hats, animals and more. She was very good at it and she showed her designs to everyone. She was proud of her work and wanted to be a designer when she grew up.

One day, she had an exam at school. The teacher asked the children to design a picture of their family. Lily was excited and started to draw and cut and stick. She made a big and beautiful picture with many colors and details. She thought it was the best picture in the class.

When she finished, she looked around and saw what the other children had done. Some had simple drawings, some had stickers, some had photos. Lily smiled and said to herself, "My picture is much better than theirs. I am the best designer in the world."

She went to the teacher and gave her the picture. The teacher looked at it and said, "Wow, Lily, this is a very nice picture. You are very talented. But can you tell me who is in your family?"

Lily pointed to the picture and said, "This is me, this is my mom, this is my dad, this is my brother, this is my dog, this is my cat, this is my fish, this is my bird, this is my hamster, this is my turtle, this is my doll, this is my teddy bear, this is my robot, this is my unicorn, this is my fairy, this is my dragon, this is my castle, this is my rainbow, this is my star, this is my moon, this is my sun, this is my flower, this is my heart, this is my name."

The teacher was surprised and said, "Lily, that is a lot of things. But are they all in your family? Do you really have a unicorn, a fairy, a dragon, a castle, a rainbow, a star, a moon, a sun, a flower and a heart?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, they are all in my family. They are all in my imagination. I love them all and they love me. They make me happy and they help me design things."

The teacher smiled and said, "Lily, I am glad that you have a rich imagination and that you love to design things. But you know, a family is not only what you imagine. A family is also what you have in real life. A family is the people who care for you, who support you, who teach you, who play with you, who hug you, who listen to you, who share with you, who laugh with you, who cry with you, who forgive you, who respect you, who love you. A family is not only what you see, but also what you feel. Do you understand?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I understand. I love my mom, my dad, my brother, my dog and my cat. They are my real family. They are always there for me. They are more important than anything else. I am sorry, teacher, I was wrong. I was not humble. I was selfish and proud. I wanted to show off and make the best picture. But I forgot about my real family. Can I make a new picture?"

The teacher nodded and said, "Of course, Lily, you can make a new picture. And I am proud of you for being humble and honest. You are not only a good designer, but also a good person. And that is what matters most."

Lily thanked the teacher and went back to her seat. She took a new paper and crayons and started to design a new picture of her family. She drew her mom, her dad, her brother, her dog and her cat. She also drew a small unicorn, a fairy, a dragon, a castle, a rainbow, a star, a moon, a sun, a flower and a heart. But she made them very small and put them in the corner of the paper. She wrote under the picture, "This is my family. I love them all. They are real and they are in my heart."

The end.

Tommy was playing with his toy cars in his room. He liked to make them zoom and crash on the floor. He did not hear his mom call him for bath time. She came to his room and saw the mess.

"Tommy, it's time for your bath. Put away your cars and come with me," she said.

"But I don't want a bath. I want to play more," Tommy said. He held his cars tight and did not move.

Mom was not happy. She took his cars and put them on the shelf. She urged Tommy to get up and follow her. She said, "You need a bath to be clean and fresh. You can play with your cars again tomorrow. Now, let's go."

Tommy was sad and angry. He did not like to leave his cars. He did not like to be wet and soapy. He walked slowly behind his mom. He hoped she would change her mind.

But she did not. She filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles. She put Tommy in the water and gave him a washcloth and a rubber duck. She said, "Look, you have a duck to play with. And the bubbles are fun. You can make shapes and pop them. Try it."

Tommy looked at the duck and the bubbles. He did not want to admit it, but they looked a little fun. He took the duck and squeezed it. It made a quack sound. He smiled. He dipped the washcloth in the water and made it wet. He threw it in the air and watched it fall. He laughed.

Mom smiled too. She said, "See, bath time is not so bad. You can have fun and be clean at the same time. Now, let me wash your hair and then you can play some more."

Tommy nodded. He let mom wash his hair and rinse it. He did not cry or fuss. He felt the water and the bubbles on his skin. He felt good. He said, "Thank you, mom. I like bath time."

Mom hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I'm proud of you. You're a good boy. Now, let's get you dry and put on your pajamas. Then we can read a story before bed."

Tommy agreed. He got out of the bathtub and wrapped himself in a towel. He felt warm and cozy. He followed mom to his room. He saw his cars on the shelf. He did not miss them so much. He was ready for bed. He said, "Mom, can you read me the story about the big red car?"

Mom said, "Of course, Tommy. I love that story. Let's go to your bed and I'll read it to you."

They went to his bed and mom opened the book. She read the story about the big red car and its adventures. Tommy listened and imagined. He felt happy and sleepy. He closed his eyes and drifted to sleep. Mom kissed him and said, "Good night, Tommy. I love you."

Tommy murmured, "I love you too, mom. Good night."

Anna and Ben gasped. They ran downstairs and out the door. They ran to the truck and asked the man if they could see the ostrich.

"Sorry, kids, this ostrich is not for you," the man said. "This ostrich is going to another zoo. He is very sick and needs a special doctor."

"Please, sir, please," they said. "We love ostriches. We just want to say hello."

The man looked at them and smiled. He was a kind man. He said, "Okay, but only for a minute. And be careful. He might bite."

He opened the cage and let them in. Anna and Ben were very happy. They touched the ostrich's feathers and looked into his eyes. The ostrich looked sad and tired. He did not bite.

"Thank you, sir, thank you," they said. "We hope he gets better soon."

They gave the ostrich a hug and said goodbye. They ran back to their mom and told her what they saw. Mom was surprised and worried. She said, "You should not have done that, kids. That was very dangerous. What if the ostrich had hurt you? Or what if he had a disease that you could catch?"

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They did not mean to be bad. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We just wanted to see the ostrich. He was very nice. He did not hurt us. He did not have a disease. He was just sick."

Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you're okay, kids. But next time, you have to ask me before you do something like that. And next time, we'll go to the zoo together and see the ostrich and all the other animals."

Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "Okay, mom. We love you. And we love the ostrich."

They went back to their room and drew a picture of the ostrich. They gave it to the man when he came back to the truck. The man thanked them and said, "You're very sweet, kids. The ostrich will love this. Maybe he'll feel better soon."

He drove away with the ostrich. Anna and Ben waved goodbye. They were not bored anymore. They had a new friend.

"Can we pet him?" Sara asks the man.

"Sure, if you want to," the man says. "He is friendly. He likes kids. He will not bite you."

Sara and Tom laugh. They are not scared anymore. They are happy. They make a new friend. They unite with the dog.

The man is happy too. He thanks Sara and Tom for being nice to his dog. He gives them a treat. He says goodbye and leaves with his dog.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys and run in the park. But they do not like to eat vegetables. They only want to eat cake and candy.

One day, their mom says, "Boys, I have to go to the store. I will be back soon. Please help me cook dinner. You can use the carrots in the fridge. They are good for you."

Tom and Sam do not want to cook carrots. They think carrots are yucky and boring. They have a bad idea. They decide to cook the carrots very fast. They put all the carrots in a big pot. They turn on the stove to the highest heat. They think the carrots will be done in a minute.

But they are wrong. The carrots start to burn. The pot makes a loud noise. Smoke comes out of the pot. The smoke alarm beeps. Tom and Sam are scared. They run out of the kitchen.

Their mom comes back. She sees the mess. She is angry and sad. She says, "Boys, what did you do? You could have started a fire. You could have hurt yourselves. You did not listen to me. You did not cook the carrots properly. You wasted good food. You have to learn to be careful and respectful in the kitchen."

Tom and Sam feel sorry. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We did not mean to cause trouble. We just did not want to eat carrots. We thought they were yucky and boring. But we were wrong. We should have tried them. We should have cooked them slowly and gently. We should have followed your instructions. We will not do it again. Please forgive us."

Their mom hugs them. She says, "I forgive you. I love you. But you have to promise me to eat your vegetables. They are good for you. They make you strong and healthy. They are not yucky and boring. They are tasty and colorful. You can cook them in different ways. You can add some salt, pepper, butter, cheese, or sauce. You can make them into soup, salad, pie, or cake. You can have fun with them. You just have to try them."

Tom and Sam nod. They say, "We promise. We will eat our vegetables. We will try them. We will cook them in different ways. We will have fun with them. Thank you, mom."

Their mom smiles. She says, "You are welcome, boys. Now, let's clean up the kitchen. And then, let's make a new dinner. How about some carrot cake?"

Tom and Sam cheer. They say, "Yes, please. We love carrot cake. Carrots are not so bad after all. They are good for us. And they are good for cake."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be careful and respectful in the kitchen, to listen to their parents, to eat their vegetables, and to try new things.

His dad helped him reel in the fish. It was a big one! Timmy was so happy that he caught a fish. He said, "Dad, can we keep the fish?" His dad replied, "Sure, but we have to cook it first." 

At the end of the day, Timmy and his dad took the fish home and cooked it for dinner. It was delicious! Timmy was glad that he caught a fish and that it was available for them to eat.

As Lily was running, she saw her friend, the squirrel, up in a tree. She stopped to say hello. They both looked at the beautiful garden and smiled. They were happy to live in such a lovely place. And then, they continued to play and run in the beautiful garden all day long.

"Hi Sam!" said Ben. "Do you want to play with me today?" Sam looked at Ben and said, "I would love to play, but I smell something funny. It smells like fire."

Ben and Sam went to find what the smell was. They walked and walked until they saw smoke. They found a small fire near a tree. Ben and Sam were scared, but they knew they had to put the fire out.

They worked together to get water from the nearby river. Ben used his strong legs to spring back and forth, carrying water in big leaves. Sam used his wings to fan the fire to keep it small. Soon, the fire was out, and the woods were safe again.

Ben and Sam were happy they could help. They spent the rest of the day playing in the woods, knowing that they had saved their home from the fire.

Later, Sam and Billy saw a big bird. The bird wanted to eat Billy. Sam had an idea. He used his cobweb to trap the bird. The bird could not eat Billy now. Sam saved Billy with his cobweb. They were happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a family who had a hard time telling when one thing ended and when something else began. They had no calendar, so they never knew which day was which.

One day, something strange appeared in the family's house. It was a calendar! They were very surprised and excited by this new thing. 

The family decided to start using the calendar to keep track of the days. This worked really well for a while. But then, the family found something hard about following a calendar. They realized that if they devoted all their time to keeping track of what the calendar said, they would miss out on all the fun things life has to offer. 

So the family decided to use the calendar just to know what day it was, but not to always plan every minute of their day according to the calendar. This decision made them happy and meant they had more time to spend together.

The moral of the story is that even though calendars can be helpful sometimes, it's still important to make time for fun and family.

The girl approached the old man and said, "Hello?" The old man turned and smiled a gentle, kind smile. He reached into his pocket and pulled out an envelope. He handed the envelope to the girl and said, "This is for you, my dear."

The girl was so excited. She wanted to open the envelope and find out what was inside. But the old man seemed so wise. He just smiled and said, "Wait until you get home. When you open it, your life will be changed forever."

The girl scurried off to her home, her heart racing with anticipation. When she arrived, she carefully opened the envelope and inside, she found a beautiful gift - a beautiful butterfly. It had been sent to her from the old man in the park.

The girl had been foreshadowed. Even though the old man's words had seemed mysterious, she now understood the true meaning. It was a gift of peace, hope and love - a life-changing gift from a kind and gentle soul. She kept the butterfly with her always; it was a reminder that no matter what, love was always around her.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant who lived in the forest. One day, he was feeling very curious, so he decided to try to weigh himself. He stretched his trunk up as high as he could and found a very big rock. He put one side of the rock on one side of his trunk, and the other side of the rock on the other side of his trunk. Then he stepped on the rock to balance it. He closed his eyes and tried to weigh himself. To his surprise, he was the same weight on both sides! He was so happy, he wanted to show everyone.

So the elephant shouted to all of the animals in the forest, "Come and see how I weighed myself!" All of the animals gathered around the elephant to see how he had weighed himself. They were all so impressed! The elephant explained that he had used a big open rock to weigh himself, and that it had worked!

Everyone cheered in the forest and the elephant was so proud. From that day on, the elephant would always weigh himself with the big open rock whenever he wanted to check if he was the same weight. The end.

The sunflower had grown from a tiny seed that the farmer had forgotten to put in the ground. And now he had a giant tall sunflower in the middle of his wheat field!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Tina who was celebrating her 3rd birthday. All of her friends and family had gathered to help her celebrate when suddenly they smelled something burning. 

Tina quickly ran to the kitchen and saw that a pot of boiling water was bubbling over and spreading a black smoke. Everyone in the room started to panic and shouted, "What do we do?!"

Tina was very persistent and knew what to do! She grabbed a measuring cup, scooped up a cup of water and threw it on the stove.

The water extinguished the flames and everyone cheered. Tina was happy that she could help save the day. But when she turned around all of her friends and family had disappeared. 

She sighed and started to clean up the mess. That's when she noticed something had been written on the kitchen wall. It said, "If you measure up to the challenge, it will be your last birthday." 

Tina had never felt so scared in her life. She had unknowingly solved a magical riddle and now she was cursed! Every year on her birthday, something bad would happen unless she found a way to break the curse. 

Tina was persistent and never gave up, but despite her best efforts, she never had any luck. And in the end the curse still haunted her and it became a sad ending.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who liked to spend his days fishing in the river. One day, he was getting ready to go fishing when he heard a sound and saw a baby bird, who had become separated from its mommy. The old man was kind and thought it was a silly, helpless bird, so he decided to attach it to his hat. 

He started to walk to the river and the bird with him. As he walked, he talked to the bird, saying small things like hello and how he was feeling that day. The bird was quiet and didn't talk back, but the old man thought that was okay.

When he got to the river, the old man sat down and started to fish. But, he was too stupid to realize that the bird's feet were stuck to the hat and the bird couldn't fly away.

The sun was coming down, and the old man never noticed the bird was still stuck on the hat. The poor bird chirped softly until all its energy was gone and it could not chirp anymore. 

The old man never knew what happened to the bird, he just left the river with the hat on his head and the poor bird gone forever.

The two kids thought about it and decided he wasn't so scary. They agreed to be his friends and invited him to play in their garden every day.

From then on, the flea spent his days playing with his new friends. The flea was no longer lonely and he was so happy. He always listened to his friends very carefully and they always had fun!

Suddenly, her mom shouted, "Lucy! I forgot the spaghetti at home!" Lucy was so sad. She wanted to eat spaghetti so badly! 

But then her mom smiled. She had an idea! She took Lucy's hat and filled it with the icy snow. Then, she said, "Lucy, close your eyes and pretend this snow is spaghetti!"

The End.

Now, Lily could kick the icy pond without feeling cold. The fairy and Lily played all day, kicking the ice and laughing. They had so much fun together. And from that day on, they knew that they would always be the best of friends.

In the story, there was a big, strong lion. The lion was very serious and never smiled. One day, something funny happened. The lion was walking in the forest when he stepped on a banana peel. The lion slipped and fell on his back. All the animals in the forest saw this and started to laugh.

The serious lion felt a little embarrassed, but then he started to laugh too. He realized that it was okay to be silly sometimes. From that day on, the lion smiled and laughed with his friends. And Lily learned that even serious people can have fun. She liked the story and smiled too.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big box. They want to make a house with the box.

Sara says, "I will be the lawyer. I will help people with their problems."

Tom says, "No, I will be the lawyer. You can be the cook. You can make food for me."

Sara says, "No, that is not fair. I want to be the lawyer too. You can be the doctor. You can make people feel better."

Tom says, "No, I don't want to be the doctor. I want to be the lawyer. You can be the teacher. You can make people learn."

Sara and Tom start to argue. They push and pull the box. They are not happy.

A man comes to the park. He is a real lawyer. He sees Sara and Tom fighting. He says, "Hello, children. Why are you fighting?"

Sara and Tom stop fighting. They look at the man. They say, "We want to be lawyers. But we only have one box."

The man says, "I see. Being a lawyer is a good job. But you don't need a box to be a lawyer. You need a book and a pen. You can read and write and learn the law. You can share the book and the pen. Then you can both be lawyers."

Sara and Tom think. They say, "That sounds good. Thank you, sir. Can we have a book and a pen?"

The man says, "Sure. I have a book and a pen in my car. I will give them to you. But you have to promise me something. You have to be kind and honest and help people. That is what a good lawyer does."

Sara and Tom say, "We promise. We will be kind and honest and help people."

The man smiles. He says, "Good. Then follow me. I will give you the book and the pen. And maybe some cookies too. They are mild and sweet. Just like you."

One day, they go to the park. The park has grass, trees, flowers and a pond. Tim and Spot enjoy running and playing in the park. They chase a ball, sniff the flowers and splash in the pond. They are happy.

But then, they see an elderly lady. She is walking with a cane and a small dog. The small dog is white and fluffy and has a pink bow on its head. The small dog barks at Spot. Spot barks back. The elderly lady gets scared. She tries to pull the small dog away, but the small dog bites Spot's heel. Spot yelps. Tim runs to help him.

Tim is angry at the small dog. He says, "Bad dog! Why did you bite Spot? He is not mean. He just wanted to play. You hurt him. You are not nice." The elderly lady is sorry. She says, "I'm sorry, little boy. My dog is not friendly. She is old and grumpy. She doesn't like other dogs. I should have kept her on a leash. I hope your dog is okay."

Tim looks at Spot's heel. It is red and sore, but not bleeding. He says, "Spot is okay. He is brave and strong. But he needs a hug. And a treat." The elderly lady smiles. She says, "You are a good boy. And your dog is a good dog. Here, have a cookie. And give one to your dog, too. I hope you have a nice day." She gives Tim and Spot a cookie each and walks away with her small dog.

Tim and Spot eat their cookies. They are sweet and crunchy. They thank the elderly lady. They are not angry anymore. They are friends. They enjoy the rest of their walk. They are happy.

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a big pond with many ducks and swans. Ben liked the ducks, but Lily liked the swans. She saw a white swan with a long neck and a black beak. She wanted to touch it.

"Can I touch the swan, Mom?" Lily asked.

"No, honey, the swan might bite you. Swans are not very friendly. They like to be alone," Mom said.

"But the swan is so pretty. And it looks soft and fluffy," Lily said.

She walked closer to the pond. The swan saw her and swam to the edge. It looked at Lily with its small eyes. Lily reached out her hand to pet the swan.

"Quack, quack!" Ben shouted. He threw some bread to the ducks. The ducks came to him and ate the bread. Ben laughed and clapped his hands.

The swan heard Ben and turned its head. It saw the ducks and the bread. It wanted some too. It left Lily and swam to Ben. It opened its beak and snapped at the ducks. The ducks got scared and flew away. The swan ate the bread.

Lily felt sad. She thought the swan liked her. She wanted to be its friend. She ran to Mom and hugged her.

"Mom, the swan is mean. It left me and chased the ducks. It doesn't want to play with me," Lily said.

Mom hugged Lily and kissed her cheek.

"I'm sorry, honey. The swan is not a good friend. It is greedy and selfish. It only cares about itself. You don't need the swan. You have me and Ben. We love you and we are dependable. We will always be with you and play with you," Mom said.

Lily smiled and nodded. She felt better. She looked at Ben and saw him lay on the grass. He was tired from feeding the ducks. He closed his eyes and yawned.

"Can we lay with Ben, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. Let's lay with Ben and rest. We can watch the clouds and the birds. Maybe we will see a nice swan that is friendly and kind," Mom said.

They lay with Ben on the grass. They saw the blue sky and the white clouds. They saw a yellow bird and a red bird. They saw a black swan and a brown swan. They were happy and peaceful. They forgot about the mean white swan. They didn't need it. They had each other.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a bike. They take turns to kick the ball and ride the bike.

One day, they see a big tree in the park. The tree has many green leaves and red flowers. Tom and Lily think the tree is pretty. They want to see the flowers up close.

"Can we climb the tree?" Tom asks Lily.

"I don't know. The tree is very high. We are very small." Lily says.

"Maybe we can grow bigger. Then we can reach the flowers." Tom says.

"How can we grow bigger?" Lily asks.

Tom thinks for a moment. He has an idea.

"I know! We can zoom on the bike. Zooming makes us fast. Maybe it also makes us big." Tom says.

"OK. Let's try it." Lily says.

They run to the bike. Tom gets on the bike and Lily sits behind him. They pedal hard and zoom around the park. They zoom past the swings, the slide, the bench and the fountain. They feel the wind in their hair and the sun on their skin. They laugh and shout.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom! We are growing bigger!" Tom says.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom! We are almost there!" Lily says.

They zoom towards the tree. They see the flowers shining in the light. They stretch their arms and try to touch them. But they are still too far.

"Oh no! We are not big enough!" Tom says.

"Maybe we need to zoom more." Lily says.

They zoom faster and faster. They zoom so fast that they don't see the rock on the path. The bike hits the rock and flips over. Tom and Lily fall off the bike and land on the grass. They are not hurt, but they are dirty and sad.

They look at the bike. The bike is broken. The wheel is bent and the chain is loose. They can't zoom anymore.

They look at the tree. The tree is still high. The flowers are still out of reach. They can't grow anymore.

They start to cry. They cry loud and hard. They cry so loud that they don't hear the voice.

"Hello, little ones. Why are you crying?" The voice says.

Tom and Lily stop crying and look up. They see a friendly face. The face is smiling and kind. The face belongs to the tree.

The tree is talking to them.

Tom and Lily are surprised. They have never heard a tree talk before.

"Are you the tree?" Tom asks.

"Yes, I am the tree. And you are Tom and Lily, right?" The tree says.

"Yes, we are. How do you know our names?" Lily asks.

"I know many things. I have been here for a long time. I have seen many children play in the park. I have heard many stories and songs. I have learned many words and names. And I have watched you grow." The tree says.

"You have watched us grow?" Tom and Lily say.

"Yes, I have. I have watched you grow from babies to toddlers to children. I have watched you learn to walk, to talk, to play, to zoom. I have watched you grow bigger and smarter and happier. And I have grown fond of you." The tree says.

"You have grown fond of us?" Tom and Lily say.

"Yes, I have. You are my friends. You are friendly and curious and brave. You make me happy. You make me feel alive. And I want to make you happy too." The tree says.

"You do?" Tom and Lily say.

"Yes, I do. That's why I want to give you a gift. A gift of flowers. The flowers that you wanted to see and touch. The flowers that you tried to reach by zooming and growing. The flowers that are my pride and joy." The tree says.

The tree shakes its branches. The red flowers fall from the tree and land on the grass. They form a carpet of color and scent. They cover Tom and Lily and the bike.

Tom and Lily are amazed. They see the flowers up close. They smell the flowers. They touch the flowers. They feel the flowers. The flowers are soft and sweet and beautiful.

They look at the tree. The tree is smiling and kind. The tree is their friend.

They smile back at the tree. They say thank you to the tree. They hug the tree.

They are happy. They are happy with the flowers. They are happy with the tree. They are happy with each other.

They don't need to zoom anymore. They don't need to grow anymore. They have everything they need.

They have friendship.

"I saw it first, Anna. It is mine. Give it to me," Ben says.

"No, Ben. I saw it first. It is mine. Let go of it," Anna says.

They start to pull the button from each other. They do not share. They do not listen. They do not care. They only want the button.

Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They have no button. They have no thread. They have no necklaces and bracelets. They have no fun.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the closet. She sees the mess and the tears. She knows what happened.

Mom smiles and says, "That's good, Anna and Ben. I love you too. Now, let's clean up this mess and make new necklaces and bracelets. But this time, let's use a thicker thread and a smaller button. And let's make one for each other. How does that sound?"

"Not today, Mimi. It is not safe out there. There are big cats and dogs and birds that want to eat you. You must stay underground with me and your brothers and sisters." Mama mouse said.

"But mama, I want to see the sun and the flowers and the trees. I want to have fun and make new friends. Please, mama, please." Mimi begged.

Mama mouse sighed. She loved Mimi very much and wanted her to be happy, but she also wanted her to be safe. She thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, Mimi. You can go out for a little while, but you must promise me three things. First, you must not go too far from the hole. Second, you must not talk to any strangers. And third, you must come back before it gets dark. Do you understand?"

"Yes, mama. I understand. I promise. Thank you, mama. I love you." Mimi said. She gave her mama a big hug and then ran out of the hole.

"That was very nice of you, Lily," Lily's mom said. "You know, that tomato is very unique. It is from a special seed that your grandma sent me. She grew it in her garden, too. She said it is very tasty and healthy."

"Really?" Lily said. "That's cool!"

"Yes, it is," Lily's mom said. "Do you want to add it to the salad?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They put their tomato halves in the bowl and mixed them with the lettuce, cheese, and dressing.

"Yum, this looks good!" Ben said.

"It does," Lily said. "Let's eat!"

They sat down at the table and enjoyed their lunch. They thanked Lily's mom and grandma for the unique tomato. They were happy and full.
