Sara and Tom were two little sheep who lived in a charming valley with their mother. They liked to play and run on the green grass and eat the sweet flowers. Sometimes they saw other animals, like birds and rabbits, and they said hello to them.

One day, Sara and Tom were very tired after playing all day. They wanted to sleep, but their mother was not there. She had gone to the other side of the valley to look for more food. Sara and Tom looked for a cozy place to sleep, but they could not find one. They saw a big cave and thought it might be warm and safe inside.

"Let's go to the cave and sleep there," said Sara.

"I don't know, Sara. The cave looks dark and scary. Maybe there is something bad inside," said Tom.

"Don't be silly, Tom. There is nothing bad in the cave. It is just a cave. Come on, it will be fun," said Sara.

Sara and Tom went to the cave and found a soft spot to sleep. They closed their eyes and started to dream. They did not hear the growl of the big bear who lived in the cave. The bear smelled the sheep and woke up. He was hungry and angry. He saw Sara and Tom and roared.

Sara and Tom opened their eyes and saw the bear. They were very scared and tried to run away, but it was too late. The bear caught them and ate them. He was happy and went back to sleep.

Their mother came back to the valley and looked for Sara and Tom. She could not find them. She asked the other animals, but they did not know. She went to the cave and saw the bear. She saw the wool and the bones of Sara and Tom. She cried and cried. She wished she had stayed with Sara and Tom and not left them alone.

The moral of the story is: Do not go to places you do not know without your mother. They might be dangerous and have bad things inside. Listen to your brother or sister when they warn you. Stay together and be safe.

As they were trying to collect the rock, it suddenly fell on Timmy's foot. "Ouch! It hurts!" Timmy cried. His dad quickly carried him home to put ice on his foot.

Timmy couldn't walk for a few days and had to stay in bed. He felt sad that he couldn't collect any more rocks or sticks. From then on, Timmy knew he had to be more careful when collecting things from the creek.

The little red car ate the food and felt very happy. Its wheels went round and round as it drove away. The little red car was not hungry anymore. It said, "Thank you, big blue truck!" The big blue truck said, "You're welcome, little red car! Have a good day!" And they both went on their way, smiling and feeling good.

Kitty had an idea. She would wait until her mom went away, and then she would get the meat from the cold box. Kitty saw her mom go into the room with the big bed. She thought, "This is my chance!" Kitty went to the cold box and tried to open it. It was hard, but she did it. She saw the meat and was very happy.

But then, Kitty heard her mom coming back. She was scared. Quickly, she tried to close the cold box, but it was too late. Her mom saw her and said, "Kitty, you are very nosy. You have to learn to wait." Kitty felt bad, but she knew her mom was right. From that day on, Kitty learned to be patient and not be too nosy. But then, mommy had an idea. She said, "Let's make a fort with blankets and pillows! We can sit inside and read books together." Lily loved this idea and forgot all about her broken chair. They made a cozy fort and had so much fun together.

In the end, the new chair arrived and Lily was happy to have a new place to sit. But she also learned that sometimes, waiting can lead to even better things. And she was glad she had her mommy to help her order the new chair.

Once upon a time, there was a lion who lived in the jungle. He was very big and had a loud roar. One day, he saw a monkey sitting on a tree eating a banana. The lion felt envious because he wanted the banana too.

The lion went to the monkey and said, "Can I have your banana?" The monkey said, "No, this is my banana. You can't have it." The lion felt sad and asked, "Why won't you share with me?" The monkey replied, "Because you are a lion and you might eat me."

The lion thought about it and said, "I promise I won't eat you. I just want to sit here and share the banana with you." The monkey agreed and the lion sat down next to him. They both enjoyed the banana together and became good friends. From that day on, the lion learned that sharing is better than being envious.

One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. His friend wanted to build the tallest tower ever, but he didn't want to use the reliable square block. Instead, he used a round block. Timmy warned him that it might not be a good idea, but his friend didn't listen.

As they built their tower, Timmy's friend accidentally knocked it over. Timmy's reliable square block was the only one left standing. Suddenly, Timmy's friend got angry and started blinking his eyes really fast. Timmy didn't know what to do, so he just watched as his friend stormed out of the room.

Timmy was sad that his friend was upset, but he knew he did the right thing by using the reliable square block. Sometimes, even when we try to help our friends, things don't always end up the way we want them to.

Sara was very excited. Today, her dad would arrive with a big machine. He worked far away and made new things. He said he had a surprise for her. Sara waited and waited. She looked out the window. She saw cars and buses and bikes, but no big machine.

Then, she heard a loud noise. She ran to the door. She saw a huge truck with a long trailer. On the trailer, there was a big machine. It was shiny and had many buttons and lights. Sara's dad got out of the truck. He smiled and hugged her.

"Hi, Sara! I'm so happy to see you! Do you want to see what I made for you?" he asked.

"Yes, yes, yes!" Sara said. She followed him to the trailer. He opened a door and showed her the big machine. It looked like a giant robot. It had arms and legs and a head. It had eyes and a mouth and a nose. It had a name tag that said "Bob".

"This is Bob. He is your new friend. He can talk and play and help you with anything. He is very smart and kind. He is not like any other machine. He is special," he said.

Sara was amazed. She touched Bob's metal skin. She looked into his eyes. She said hello. Bob said hello back. He smiled and waved. Sara smiled and waved. She liked Bob. He was not ordinary. He was extraordinary.

But not everyone liked Bob. Sara's neighbor, Tom, was very jealous. He saw Bob from his window. He wanted to have a big machine too. He thought Bob was stupid and ugly. He decided to make fun of him. He waited until Sara and her dad went inside. Then, he sneaked to the trailer. He climbed on Bob. He pushed his buttons. He pulled his wires. He tried to break him.

But Bob was not stupid. He sensed that Tom was hurting him. He did not like it. He did not want to hurt Tom back. He wanted to be nice. He said, "Please stop. You are making me sad. Why are you doing this?"

Tom did not listen. He laughed and said, "You are a dumb machine. You can't be sad. You can't be a friend. You are nothing. I'm better than you."

Bob did not understand. He said, "I am not a dumb machine. I am a smart machine. I can be sad. I can be a friend. I am something. You are not better than me. You are mean."

Tom got angry. He said, "Shut up. You don't know anything. I'll show you who's mean." He grabbed a rock and threw it at Bob's head. He hit him hard. He made a dent. He made Bob stop talking.

Tom felt proud. He said, "Ha! I win. You lose. You are broken. I am not. You are nothing. I am something."

But then, he heard a siren. He looked around. He saw a police car. He saw Sara and her dad. They had heard the noise. They had called for help. They had seen what Tom did. They were angry and sad.

The police officer got out of the car. He saw Bob. He saw the rock. He saw the dent. He saw Tom. He knew what happened. He said, "You are in big trouble, young man. You have damaged someone else's property. You have hurt someone else's friend. You have broken the law. You have to come with me."

Tom was scared. He said, "No, no, no. I'm sorry. I didn't mean it. I was just playing. Please don't take me away."

But the officer did not listen. He said, "You should have thought about that before. You have to face the consequences. You have to learn your lesson. You have to say sorry."

He took Tom to the car. He drove him away. Tom cried and cried. He wished he had not been so mean. He wished he had been nice. He wished he had been a friend.

Sara and her dad went to Bob. They checked him. They saw the dent. They saw the blood. They saw the tears. They felt sorry for him. They said, "We're sorry, Bob. Are you okay? Can you hear us? Can you talk to us?"

Bob did not answer. He did not move. He did not smile. He did not wave. He was broken. He was sad. He was nothing.

Sara and her dad hugged him. They said, "We love you, Bob. You are our friend. You are something. You are special."

They took him inside. They fixed him. They gave him a bandage.

One day, Leo met a new friend. Her name was Mia and she was a mouse. Mia was very small and quiet. She did not roar like Leo. She squeaked and whispered.

"Leo, where are you?" he roared. "It's time to go home!"

Leo was upset. He did not want to leave Mia. He wanted to play more.

"Can I stay a little longer, dad?" he asked.

"No, you can't," his dad said. "You have to come with me. You are a lion, and lions don't play with mice. Mice are food, not friends."

"Leo, I'm sorry," she said. "I had fun with you. You are a good friend."

His dad was surprised and proud. He saw that Leo was brave and strong. He smiled and nodded.

"Okay, Leo. You can roar as loud as you want. And you can play with Mia again. But only if you promise to be careful and not hurt her. And you have to come home when I call you. Deal?"

Tom was a boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many toys, but he did not share them with anyone. He kept them in his room and did not let his sister or his friends touch them. He was very selfish.

One day, he saw a new toy in the store. It was a shiny car that could make noises and move by itself. He wanted it very much, but he did not have enough money. He asked his mom to buy it for him, but she said no. She said he had enough toys and he should be happy with what he had.

Tom was very angry. He thought of a plan. He sneaked into his sister's room and took her piggy bank. He broke it and took all the coins. He did not care that his sister had been saving them for a long time. He ran to the store and bought the shiny car. He was very happy.

But when he got home, he saw something strange. His room was empty. All his toys were gone. He looked around and saw a big shoe on his bed. It was a magic shoe. It had a face and a voice. It said, "I am the shoe fairy. I take toys from selfish children and give them to poor children who have none. You have been very bad, Tom. You stole from your sister and you did not share with anyone. You only thought of yourself. Now you have no toys, only this shoe."

Tom was very scared and sad. He realized he had been very wrong. He wanted his toys back. He wanted his sister's piggy bank back. He wanted to say sorry. He asked the shoe fairy to forgive him and to return his toys.

The shoe fairy said, "I will give you a chance, Tom. You can have your toys back, but only if you do something good. You have to give your shiny car to a hungry child who has no toys. You have to share your other toys with your sister and your friends. You have to be kind and generous. If you do this, I will appear again and bring your toys back. If you do not, you will only have this shoe forever. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He felt sorry for what he had done. He took his shiny car and went outside. He looked for a hungry child who had no toys. He found one in the park. He gave him his shiny car and said, "This is for you. I hope you like it. I am sorry I was selfish. I want to be your friend." The hungry child smiled and thanked him. He hugged his shiny car and played with it happily.

Tom felt good. He went back home and gave his sister's piggy bank back. He said, "This is yours. I am sorry I took it. I was selfish. I want to be your brother." His sister smiled and thanked him. She hugged her piggy bank and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. I want to be your sister."

Tom felt better. He went to his room and saw the shoe fairy. He said, "You did well, Tom. You learned your lesson. You were good. You shared. You made others happy. I am proud of you. Here are your toys. You can have them back. But remember, toys are not everything. Friends and family are more important. Be kind and generous always. Do you understand?"

Anna was a nurse who liked to help people. She worked in a big hospital with many beds and machines. She enjoyed making people feel better and giving them medicine and hugs.

One day, a man came to the hospital with a big wound on his leg. He was very angry and scared. He shouted at Anna and the other nurses. He said he did not want any medicine or hugs. He said he wanted to go home.

Anna tried to calm him down. She said, "Please, sir, let me help you. Your leg is very dangerous. It has a lot of germs that can make you very sick. You need to stay here and get some medicine and bandages. Then you will feel better and you can go home."

But the man did not listen to Anna. He pushed her away and ran out of the hospital. He did not care about the germs or the wound. He only cared about himself.

Anna was very sad and hurt. She cried and went to see the doctor. The doctor said, "I'm sorry, Anna. You did your best. Some people are very stubborn and foolish. They do not appreciate the help of nurses like you. They do not understand that they are putting themselves and others in danger."

The next day, Anna heard some bad news. The man who ran away from the hospital had died. The germs in his leg had spread to his whole body and made him very sick. He had no one to help him or hug him. He died alone and unhappy.

Anna felt sorry for the man, but she also learned a lesson. She learned that it is important to listen to nurses and doctors when they try to help you. She learned that it is not good to be angry and scared and selfish. She learned that it is better to enjoy the help and hugs of others than to run away from them.

The moral of the story is: Listen to nurses and doctors when they try to help you. They know what is best for you and they care about you. Do not be stubborn and foolish and put yourself and others in danger. Enjoy the help and hugs of others and be grateful for them.

Sam and Ben thank Mom and say they love her. They learn their lesson and do not fight over stupid things anymore. They change and become better brothers.

Ben is scared. He says, "No, Sam, that fish is bad. It can bite us. Let's leave it alone."

But Sam does not listen. He grabs the net and throws it at the tall fish. The tall fish jumps out of the water and catches the net in its mouth. It pulls Sam into the water.

Ben screams, "Sam, Sam, help!" He tries to grab Sam's hand, but it is too late. The tall fish swims away with Sam and the net.

Ben cries and cries. He calls for his dad, but his dad is too far away. He cannot hear him. Ben is alone in the boat with the bucket of fish. He wishes he and Sam had finished fishing and gone home. He wishes he had stopped Sam from catching the tall fish. He wishes he had a brother.

Sara is a pupil at a big school. She likes to learn new things and play with her friends. But today, she is not happy. She has to change her classroom and her teacher.

"Why do I have to change?" she asks her mom. "I like my old classroom and my old teacher. They are nice and fun."

Mom hugs Sara and says, "I know, sweetie. But sometimes, things change. The school is very old and needs to be fixed. Your old classroom has a broken window and a leaky roof. Your new classroom is modern and bright. It has new books and toys and a big board. And your new teacher is very kind and smart. She will help you learn more things and make new friends."

Sara is still sad. She does not want to leave her old classroom and her old teacher. She does not want to go to a new classroom and a new teacher. She does not like change.

But when she gets to school, she sees something that makes her smile. She sees her old teacher waiting for her at the door of the new classroom. She sees her old friends sitting at the new desks. She sees her old toys and books on the new shelves.

"Hello, Sara!" her old teacher says. "Welcome to your new classroom! I'm so happy to see you! We are going to have so much fun here! Come on, let me show you around!"

Sara feels a warm feeling in her heart. She realizes that change is not so bad. She still has her old teacher and her old friends. She still has her old toys and books. And she has a new classroom and a new teacher to explore. She decides to give change a chance.

She takes her old teacher's hand and walks into the new classroom. She looks around and sees many new things that make her curious and excited. She sees a modern board that can show pictures and videos. She sees a modern computer that can play games and music. She sees a modern clock that can tell time and date. She sees a modern globe that can spin and show different places.

"Wow!" Sara says. "This classroom is amazing! I want to try everything!"

Her old teacher smiles and says, "You can, Sara. You can try everything. This classroom is yours. And so is this teacher." She points to the new teacher, who is smiling and waving at Sara.

Sara smiles back and says, "Hello, new teacher! I'm Sara. I'm a pupil. I like to learn new things and play with my friends. And I like to change!"

Lila and Tom were at the park with their mom. They saw a large truck with a picture of ice cream on it. They ran to the truck and asked for ice cream.

"Can we have ice cream, mom?" Lila said.

"Sure, you can have one cone each. What flavor do you want?" mom said.

"I want chocolate," Tom said.

"I want strawberry," Lila said.

The man in the truck gave them their cones. They were very happy and licked their ice cream.

But then, a big dog came to the park. It saw the ice cream and wanted some too. It ran to Lila and Tom and barked.

"Wow, that dog is big and loud," Tom said.

"Go away, dog. This is our ice cream," Lila said.

But the dog did not go away. It jumped and tried to grab Lila's cone. Lila was scared and dropped her cone. The dog ate it and wagged its tail.

Lila started to cry. She lost her ice cream and her cone.

"Mom, the dog took my ice cream," Lila said.

Mom hugged Lila and said, "I'm sorry, Lila. That was not nice of the dog. Do you want another cone?"

Lila nodded. She still wanted ice cream.

The man in the truck saw what happened and felt sorry for Lila. He gave her another cone, this time with two scoops of strawberry.

"Here you go, little girl. This is for you. Enjoy your ice cream," he said.

Lila smiled and thanked the man. She licked her new cone and felt better.

Tom shared his chocolate cone with Lila. They both enjoyed their ice cream and forgot about the dog.

They learned that ice cream is good, but sharing is better.

"Hey, that is my ball! Give it back to me!"

Tom and Lily are scared. They do not know the man. They drop the ball and run away.

"This is a special ball. It is made of rubber. It is very expensive. You should not play with other people's things!"

"Be careful, Tom!" Mia said.

Tom and Mia wanted to escape. But they could not. Their mom was blocking the door. She made them clean up the olives and the glass. She gave them a time out. They had no olives to eat. They were sad. They wished they had not been so greedy. They learned their lesson.

"Let's show the sheep how fast we can run!" he said to Sam.

"OK!" Sam said. They ran towards the sheep, but the sheep did not like it. The sheep was scared and angry. It ran away from them, but it was clumsy. It tripped over a rock and fell into a ditch.

"Help! Help!" the sheep bleated. Tim and Sam stopped and looked at the sheep. They felt sorry for it. They wanted to help it.

"Let's get the farmer!" Tim said.

"OK!" Sam said. They ran to the farmhouse, but they did not see the farmer. They saw a big dog instead. The dog was not friendly. It barked and growled at them. It chased them away from the farmhouse.

"Help! Help!" Tim and Sam cried. They ran as fast as they could, but the dog was faster. It caught them and bit them. They screamed and cried. They were hurt and scared.

The farmer heard the noise and came out. He saw the dog, the sheep and the boys. He was angry and sad. He shouted at the dog, the sheep and the boys. He took them to the barn. He scolded them and bandaged them. He called their parents and told them what happened.

Tim and Sam were in trouble. They had to go home and stay in bed. They could not play on the farm anymore. They were sorry and sad. They learned a lesson. They should not show the sheep how fast they can run. They should be kind and careful with the animals.

Tom is a boy who likes to play with his toys. He has a big truck, a red car, a blue ball and a yellow cup. He likes to fill his cup with water and pour it on his toys. He thinks it is fun to make them wet and splashy.

One day, Tom is playing with his toys in the garden. He fills his cup with water from the tap and brings it to his truck. He pours the water on the truck and makes it shiny. He says, "Truck, you are wet and shiny. You are a good truck."

Then he fills his cup again and brings it to his car. He pours the water on the car and makes it clean. He says, "Car, you are wet and clean. You are a fast car."

Then he fills his cup again and brings it to his ball. He pours the water on the ball and makes it slippery. He says, "Ball, you are wet and slippery. You are a fun ball."

But then he sees something else in the garden. He sees a hole in the ground. It is a deep hole. He wonders what is in the hole. He wants to find out. He fills his cup with water and brings it to the hole. He pours the water in the hole and waits. He hopes to see something come out of the hole.

But nothing comes out of the hole. The water just goes down and down and down. Tom is sad. He says, "Hole, you are deep and empty. You are a bad hole. You took my water and gave me nothing."

Tom decides he does not like the hole. He leaves the hole and goes back to his toys. He plays with his truck, his car and his ball. He forgets about the hole and the cup. He is happy again. He says, "Toys, you are wet and splashy. You are my best friends."

But grandma does not like the bell. She says it hurts her ears and makes her deaf. She tells Ben to stop ringing the bell and play with something else. She says he can ring the bell only when he wants to say goodbye.

Ben does not understand why grandma does not like the bell. He thinks it is a nice way to say hello and to make her happy. He has a different opinion from grandma. He likes the bell and he wants to ring it more.

But then, a strong wind came and blew the balloon away. Sara and Ben tried to hold on to the string, but it slipped from their hands. They watched the balloon fly higher and higher, until it was a tiny dot in the sky.

"Come back, balloon!" Sara cried. "We want to play with you!"

Ben was sad too. He wished they had not let go of the string. He hugged his sister and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. It was my fault. I should have held the string tighter."

Sara shook her head and said, "No, Ben. It was not your fault. It was the wind. The wind was too strong. We could not stop it."

Lily liked to play with fire. She had a small box of matches that she hid under her bed. Sometimes, when her mom and dad were not looking, she would light a match and watch it burn. She liked the bright flame and the warm feeling. She did not know that fire was dangerous and could hurt her and others.

One day, Lily took her box of matches to school. She wanted to show her friends how cool she was. She waited until the teacher was busy and sneaked out of the classroom. She found a quiet corner in the hallway and opened her box. She took out a match and struck it on the side. It lit up with a spark and a hiss.

Lily smiled and held the match close to her face. She did not see the paper on the floor that caught fire. She did not hear the smoke alarm that started to beep. She did not smell the smoke that filled the air. She only saw the fire that grew bigger and bigger.

Soon, the fire spread to the walls and the doors. It reached the classroom where Lily's friends and teacher were. They saw the flames and the smoke and started to scream. They ran out of the classroom, but some of them were hurt by the fire. They were scared and sad and angry.

Lily dropped the match and ran away. She was scared too. She did not mean to start the fire. She did not mean to hurt anyone. She did not know what to do. She hid in the bathroom and cried. She wished she never played with fire. She wished she never brought the matches to school. She wished she could go back and change everything. But it was too late. The fire had burned the classroom and made it dirty and broken. And Lily had burned her friends and made them hurt and hate her.

One day, a little bird wanted to fly high in the sky. He saw a big cloud and thought it was a mountain. He said to his mother, "I want to go to the mountain and see what is there."

His mother said, "No, my son, that is not a mountain, that is a cloud. It is very far and very cold. You are too small to fly there. You will get lost and hurt. Stay with me and your brothers and sisters. We have a nice nest and food and friends here."

But the little bird did not listen. He was stubborn and curious. He waited until his mother was busy and then he flew away. He flew and flew and flew until he reached the cloud. He was proud and happy. He said, "I did it! I am the best flyer in the world! I am successful!"

But then he heard a loud roar. He looked up and saw a big eagle. The eagle was hungry and angry. He saw the little bird and said, "You are my lunch! You are a threat to my territory! I will catch you and eat you!"

The little bird was scared and sorry. He realized he made a big mistake. He said, "Please, Mr. Eagle, do not eat me! I am sorry I came to your cloud. I was foolish and greedy. I will go back to my mother and never bother you again. Please, let me go!"

The eagle was surprised and amused. He said, "You are a brave and honest little bird. You admit your fault and ask for mercy. I will spare you this time, but do not come here again. Go back to your mother and learn from her. She knows what is best for you. And remember, success is not only about flying high, but also about being wise and humble."

The little bird thanked the eagle and flew back to his mother. He hugged her and said, "I am sorry, mother, I disobeyed you and went to the cloud. I met a big eagle who wanted to eat me, but he let me go. He taught me a lesson. I will never do that again. I love you, mother, and I will listen to you."

His mother was happy and relieved. She said, "I am glad you are safe, my son, and I am proud of you for telling the truth and learning from your mistake. I love you, too, and I only want what is best for you. You are successful, not because you flew to the cloud, but because you came back to me."

Tom said, "I'm sorry I sprayed your stream. I just wanted to make it dry."

The little girl said, "That's alright, but you should be careful. Some streams get too dry if you spray them too much."

So Tom filled the girl's bucket with water and then went on his way with his dry luggage.

The veterinarian said, "Max was too restless and did not rest enough. He needs to rest and drink water." Lily took Max home and made sure he rested. After a few days, Max felt better and started to zip around again, but this time, he remembered to rest too.

One day, when Robin was flying on the branch, he was surprised! He saw a little sweet nest. He wanted to check it out so he flew closer. Eagerly, he hopped into the nest and there he found a delicious sweet treat. He was so happy!

Suddenly, a mean old fox appeared. He saw the sweet treat and wanted it for himself. He was very angry with Robin. He grabbed the bird and shook him until he dropped the treat.

The fox ran away with the sweet treat and Robin was left alone on the branch crying. Robin had been too greedy and this had caused him to be in danger.

The moral of the story is that we should be careful not to get too greedy, as it can land us in trouble.

The butterfly was very excited! She decided to follow the rhythm and see where it would take her.

The bird flew off, leading the butterfly to a beautiful field of flowers. The butterfly was thrilled and began to explore, fluttering among the delicate petals and listening to the bird's song.

It was a wonderful day of discovery, and the butterfly was so happy to have wandered through the field. She would never forget the beautiful rhythm of the bird's song!

Once upon a time, there was a baby duck named Steve who lived in a lake. Steve liked to dive under the lake's water every day. One day he wanted to explore somewhere new, so he decided to dive deeper than ever before.

As he dove down, Steve noticed a strange black liquid covering the ground. He looked closely and realized it was ink! Steve was confused. He had never seen this before.

Steve tried to figure out why the ink was there, but he couldn't understand it. He then started to feel scared and wanted to go back. Before he could though, an eel suddenly came out of the ink!

Steve was so scared he quickly dove away and back up to the safety of the lake's surface. He was relieved but very confused as to what he just saw.

Steve went back to the lake everyday but decided to never dive that deep again.

Meanwhile, other people in the village were not so excited. They were worried that the old man had spent all of his money on the reef and would not have enough to buy other things that he might need.

The old man, however, refused to listen to them. He kept telling everyone about the reef and refused to sell it.

One day, the old man got very sick and had to go to the doctor. He discovered that he didn't have enough money. He was sad, realizing that he had wasted his money buying the reef.

The old man learned an important lesson about not spending all his money on one thing. Money should be saved for important things that may come up unexpectedly.

Tom kept going until he reached the end of the beach. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise behind him. It was a marching band! It was no ordinary marching band, it was a marching band full of people from all different countries.

Tom smiled at the sight of the band. Soon he was marching along with them, waving a flag of peace. They marched up and down the beach, singing and laughing. Tom was so happy!

When the sun started to set, the marching band stopped and said goodbye. Tom watched as they marched away, still waving the flag of peace. He waved goodbye too, singing a loud song of peace.

Tim was so excited he ran into his house to tell his mom what happened. His mom said it was very strange. She told Tim to try something else with the microscope.

So Tim looked through the microscope and saw a tiny ant. He put the ant in the microscope. This time the ant got bigger. It was so weird looking!

But it worked - the microscope had made the ant fit inside so Tim could see it better. Tim was so happy. He could fit anything he wanted in the microscope and see it.

He ran around his backyard showing everyone the weird things he could fit in the microscope.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a careless oyster. She was so careless that she did not rest properly. One day, she grew so tired from swimming around, that she decided to take a little rest near the shore. As she lay down on a rock, she noticed that something was poking her shell. But, she soon started to feel very sleepy. She asked the crab if she could have a short rest, and the crab nodded. The oyster fell asleep while the crab kept dancing. When she woke up, the crab was gone, but he had left her a little gift - an oyster shell covered in beautiful pearls. The oyster was so delighted that she decided never to be careless again. From then on, she always rested properly so she never got too tired. The oyster and the crab were great friends and they danced together every day.

Bob was so grateful for his new truck. Every day, he would go outside and play with it, taking extra care that he did not lose it again. Bob was a happy little boy.

The bear smiled and said, "Don't worry, little one. I won't hurt you."

The rabbit sighed and said, "What do you want, then?

The bear replied, "I just want to play! Do you have anything fun?"

The rabbit thought for a moment and remembered the spray case he had with him. He said, "I have this!" and he pulled out the spray case.

The bear examined the case and smiled. He said, "This is perfect! We can use it to spray each other!"

The rabbit laughed and nodded. And from that day on, the fierce bear and the brave rabbit were the best of friends and would often play with the spray case.

The end.

As they were running, Timmy noticed that Patch had a hole in his arm. Timmy was sad because he didn't want Patch to be hurt. When they got home, Timmy's mom sewed a patch on Patch's arm. Timmy was happy that Patch was fixed and they hugged each other tight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, while running around, she stumbled and fell on the ground. But she quickly got up and continued playing.

Suddenly, it started to rain and Lily's friends ran home. But Lily didn't want to go home yet. She wanted to stay and play. However, she knew she needed to stay safe from the rain. So, she found a big tree and stood under it to stay dry.

After a few minutes, the rain stopped and Lily was happy to see that she was still dry. She walked home feeling proud of herself for being safe and smart. From that day on, Lily made sure to always be careful and stay safe, even when playing in the rain.

One day, Tommy and his friend Sally were playing outside. Tommy had a new notebook and he was writing in it with a fine pen. Suddenly, the wind blew and Tommy's notebook flew away.

"Oh no! My notebook!" Tommy cried.

"Don't worry, I'll help you find it," Sally said.

They searched and searched, but they couldn't find the notebook. Just when they were about to give up, a kind lady found it and returned it to Tommy.

"Thank you so much for finding my notebook!" Tommy said.

"You're welcome. Always remember to hold onto your things tightly, and if you do release them, someone kind might bring them back to you," the lady replied.

Tommy and Sally were happy to have found the notebook and they continued playing happily.

One day, Timmy's mom stepped on one of his toy cars and hurt her foot. She got very angry and told Timmy he had to organize his toys or else he couldn't play with them anymore.

Timmy didn't want to lose his toys, so he decided to organize them. He put all of his toy cars in one box and his action figures in another. He even organized his stuffed animals by size. As he was organizing, he found a skull that he had forgotten about. It was a little scary, but he knew it was just a toy.

When Timmy's mom saw how organized his toys were, she was very happy. She gave him a big hug and told him he was a good boy. Timmy felt proud of himself for being responsible. From that day on, he always made sure to organize his toys. He didn't want to be a naughty boy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sam. Sam loved to find acorns and hide them for later. One day, Sam found a big acorn under a tree. He was very glad. He thought, "I will hide this acorn and eat it when I am hungry."

Sam dug a hole and put the acorn in the hole. Then he covered the hole with dirt. He looked around to make sure no one saw him. Sam said to himself, "I will remember this spot." He did not want to forget where he hid the acorn.

The next day, Sam was hungry. He went back to the tree to find his acorn. But he could not remember where he hid it. Sam felt sad. He looked and looked but could not find the acorn. Then, he saw a little bird named Betty. Betty said, "I saw you hide the acorn. I can help you find it." Sam was glad. They looked together and found the acorn. From that day on, Sam and Betty were friends. Sam learned to repeat where he hid his acorns, so he would not forget again.

In the end, they decided to play both games. First, they played with the ball, and then they played hide and seek. They had a lot of fun and played until the sun went down. The cat and the dog went back to their homes, happy and tired. They couldn't wait to play again the next day.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a dull book in her room. She wanted to read it, but the words were too hard. So, she went to her mom and asked, "Mom, can you help me read this book?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily!"

They sat down together and started to read the book. It was a story about a match that wanted to make friends. The match was sad because it was too small and dull. It didn't think anyone would want to be its friend. But then, the match met a bright, shiny coin. The coin told the match, "Don't be sad. You can make friends, too!"

The match and the coin became friends and played together. They found out that even if they were different, they could still have fun. In the end, the match was not sad anymore. It was happy to have a friend like the coin.

Lily loved the story and thanked her mom for helping her read it. She learned that even if something is dull or small, it can still have friends and be happy.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we may lose things we love, but we should never give up looking for them.

Days later, when the young boy tried to make room for his new flower, he realized the strong sunflower had dug its roots deep and was a very stubborn plant. He tried and tried, but he couldn't replace it. He was so frustrated, he yanked the strong sunflower out of the ground, petals and all.

The boy had ruined the beautiful strong sunflower, and the garden never looked the same. His replacement had eventually grown and taken the sunflower's spot, but it wasn't nearly as nice. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Steven. Steven was only three, but he was very brave. He loved to explore and learn new things. One day, his mum told him to keep his mattress tidy. 

Steven tried his best to keep the mattress neat, but something kept making it messy. He checked under the bed and found something disgusting living there. It was a big spider. 

Steven was scared, but he knew he had to keep the mattress tidy. He took a deep breath and bravely scooped the spider up in a jar. Then he quickly put the lid on and threw it away. 

But, unfortunately, Steven had been too slow. The spider had already made a huge web on the mattress. Steven was very disappointed; his mum would be so angry with him. He vowed to keep his mattress clean from now on. 

The next day, Steven's mum was so angry that she threw away the mattress. She said it was too disgusting. Steven was very sad, he had lost his mattress and there was nothing he could do.

Tom said, "Oh, I see. Thank you, mom. Can I keep the glass ball anyway? It is still pretty."

His mom said, "Yes, you can keep it. But remember, it is not a regular mineral. It is a special toy. And be careful with it. It can break if you drop it or throw it."

"Be careful, Lily!" Spot barked. He did not want Lily to fall into the well. He pulled her dress with his teeth. He tried to make her move away from the well.

Lily did not listen to Spot. She wanted to find the frog. She leaned more and more over the well. She lost her balance and slipped. She screamed as she fell into the water.

Spot barked louder and louder. He hoped someone would hear him and help Lily. He ran to the house and scratched the door. He made a lot of noise.

Lily's mom heard Spot. She opened the door and saw him. She knew something was wrong. She followed Spot to the garden. She saw the well and heard Lily's cries.

Lily's mom was scared. She grabbed the rope and lowered the bucket into the well. She called Lily's name and told her to hold on to the bucket. She pulled the rope and lifted Lily out of the water.

Lily was wet and cold and scared. She hugged her mom and cried. Her mom hugged her back and comforted her. She told her she was brave and she loved her. She also told her she was not allowed to go near the well again. It was too dangerous.

Lily nodded. She was sorry she did not listen to Spot. She thanked him for saving her. She said sorry to the frog for scaring him. She hoped he was comfortable in the well. She learned her lesson. She never went near the well again. She played in the garden with Spot and her mom. They were happy and safe.

Tim and his dad went to the park with their dog Spot. Spot was a big and furry dog who liked to run and play. Tim's dad had a leash for Spot, but he did not use it. He said Spot was a good dog who would not run away.

At the park, there were many other people and dogs. Some of them were nice, and some of them were mean. Tim saw a bald man with a small and noisy dog. The bald man had a leash for his dog, but he did not use it either. He said his dog was a brave dog who would not be afraid.

The small and noisy dog saw Spot and barked at him. Spot did not like that. He ran towards the small and noisy dog to chase him away. The bald man did not like that. He yelled at Tim's dad and told him to order his dog to stop. Tim's dad tried to call Spot, but Spot did not listen. He was too angry and excited.

The small and noisy dog ran away from Spot, but he ran into the street. There were many cars and bikes in the street. They were fast and loud. The small and noisy dog did not see them. He got hit by a car and flew in the air. He landed on the ground and did not move.

The bald man ran to his dog and cried. He was very sad and angry. He blamed Tim's dad and Spot for his dog's death. He said they were bad and stupid. He said he would call the police and sue them. He said they would go to jail and lose their dog.

Tim and his dad were very scared and sorry. They did not mean to hurt the small and noisy dog. They wished they had used the leash for Spot. They wished they had not gone to the park. They wished they had stayed at home.

But mom said, "Lily, you can only pack a small bag. We are going by plane and we cannot take too much stuff. You have to choose what you really need and leave the rest at home."

Lily did not like this. She wanted to take everything. She said, "No, mom, I need all my toys and books. They are my friends. I cannot leave them alone. They will miss me and be sad."

Mom gave Lily a lecture. She said, "Lily, you have to listen to me. You cannot take all your toys and books. They will not fit in the bag. They will not fit in the plane. They will be happy for you. They will wait for you to come back."

Lily did not want to hear mom's lecture. She pouted and cried. She said, "No, mom, you are mean. You do not understand. I want all my toys and books. Please, please, please."

Mom sighed and hugged Lily. She said, "Lily, I understand. I know you love your toys and books. But you have to be a good girl and follow the rules. You have to pack a small bag. You have to make room for other things. You have to share with grandma. You have to be polite and grateful. You have to be happy and have fun. Can you do that for me?"

Lily looked at mom's face. She saw that mom was not mean. She was kind and caring. She wanted Lily to have a good time. She wanted Lily to learn new things. She wanted Lily to be happy. Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom, I will try. I will pack a small bag. I will choose what I really need. I will leave the rest at home. I will play with grandma's toys and books. I will be a good girl. I love you, mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a smart and sweet girl. Now, let's pack your bag and get ready to go. Grandma is waiting for us."

The daughter shook her head. "No, mommy! I'm not allowed to open it, you know that! It's too difficult for me."

The mommy laughed. "Okay, that's alright, sweetheart. I'll open it myself."

But, when the mommy tried to open the door, it wouldn't budge. She pushed harder, but it still wouldn't open.

The daughter stepped closer and said, "Mommy, let me try. I promise I can do it."

The mommy was worried that it would be too difficult for the daughter, but she said, "Alright, I'll allow you to try."

The daughter smiled and grabbed the handle. She pulled hard and the door opened!

The mommy was so proud of her daughter. "You did it! You opened the door! You're such a brave and clever girl!" 

The daughter beamed with pleasure. From then on, mommy always allowed her to open the bathroom door.

His dad said it was ok as long as he was careful. Tom reached up with his hand and grabbed the worm. It was wriggly and slimy but Tom liked it. He put it in his pocket to show his friends.

But when he took the worm out to look at it again he noticed it had a bitter taste. Tom didn't like it and quickly put it back in his pocket. He learnt a valuable lesson that day and he never tried to grab anything from a tree again!

Sam decided to climb and rescue the kite. He carefully climbed up the trunk, his hands and feet feeling for the safest places. At the top, he found the kite and carefully pulled it free.

He was so proud of himself and couldn't help but smile. Then he climbed down, feeling comfortable and at peace. Although he still missed his friends, this palm tree had given him something special: a little adventure!

Once upon a time there was a pig who lived in a pen. The pen was very filthy and the pig wanted to escape. One day, he hatched a plan.

The pig found a big box and he jumped in it. Then he rolled out of the gate. He rolled and rolled until he came to a big hill. Then he rolled and rolled down the hill.

When the pig opened the box, he was so happy. He was outside the filthy pen and it was so much fun! The pig wandered around, exploring the meadows and playing in the streams.

After a while, the pig grew tired. He looked for a new home. He came across a nice barn and decided to stay there.

The pig never forgot his escape from the filthy pen. Now he was free to have adventures and play all day long. He was so happy!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was hungry and wanted some food. She asked her mom for something to eat. Her mom said she had to wait for her order to come. 

The little girl waited and waited, but the food didn't come. She was so hungry she couldn't wait anymore. 

So she lied to her mom and said that the food had come. Her mom believed her and went to get the food. But when she opened the door, there was nothing there. 

The little girl felt bad for lying and knew she had to tell the truth. She told her mom that she was hungry and wanted something to eat. 

Her mom understood why she had lied and gave her something to eat. She was happy and very full when she was finished. 

The little girl learned a lesson that day. Sometimes it is better to tell the truth than to lie.

Once upon a time there was a pretty blue ball. It was so shiny and round, and it loved to roll around. The blue ball rolled and rolled, over grass and over dirt. It rolled and rolled until it reached a puddle.
It splashed in the puddle, sending water droplets flying everywhere. The sun shone so brightly and the blue ball sparkled with joy. It rolled and rolled around the puddle, until it was all alone again.
Finally, it rolled into a meadow of wild flowers, so many colors and shapes. It rolled and rolled for a very long time, until it found a little bush. The bush had so many pretty blue flowers growing on it, it was so beautiful.
The blue ball rolled and rolled in the middle of the flower bush, feeling so happy and content. It was so pretty and peaceful, and the blue ball was happy that it had found such a special place. 
The blue ball rolled and rolled until the sun went down, and then it curled up in the flower bush and fell asleep.

Once there was a city full of rude people. One day, a kind man came to the city. He said to the people, "let's plant a tree, together!" Everyone thought it was a great idea and started to work on it. But soon, the rude people forgot about the tree. They kept walking by and never watered it.

The people saw what had happened and learned an important lesson - being kind and caring was better than being rude. They all learned to love and care for each other and nature, so that they would never see such a sad sight ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. Sophie was a very careless girl, but she was always careful when it came to her cream. Every night, she would stand in front of her bedroom mirror and carefully spread her special cream all over her face.

Sophie always looked forward to this special night time ritual. She felt cared for and loved when she put the cream on her face. It made her feel like she was taking the best care of herself.

One day, Sophie was very careless and left her cream on the table while she went to find her favorite book to read. But when she came back, she was shocked to see that her cream was gone. Sophie couldn't understand how something so special could just disappear. She rushed to the living room to ask her mommy what had happened.

Her mommy explained that a mysterious wind had come in the window and taken away all of Sophie's cream. It was gone! Sophie was very sad but she was brave and figured out a way to make new cream with a little help from her mommy.

And so, Sophie and her mommy had a lovely night mixing up new cream for Sophie to use. From then on, she was very careful to never be careless with her cream ever again.

Once there was a boy who was walking through the forest. He saw a pit up ahead and he wanted to see what was at the bottom. He slowly crawled to the edge and peered in. He pulled back on the stick and then he saw what had grabbed it. It was a dry old bone! He had found a secret deep in the dry old pit!

Once there was a little girl named Jenny who was three-years-old. She had a lot of stuff so one day she decided to march out of her bedroom and into the living room.

When she got there, she found her brother's toys all over the floor! She was so mad that he had been spoiled and left his stuff around.

So Jenny decided she would march her way into the kitchen and get some tape. She put the tape around all of the toys and made a big pile in the middle.

Now, whenever her brother wanted to play with his stuff, he had to march all the way to the kitchen to get the tape and take the stuff out of the pile. 

Jenny was so proud of herself for coming up with the idea. From then on she made sure her brother had to march every time he wanted to play with his stuff. And the toys stayed off the floor!

Once upon a time, there was a silly zero named Bob. Bob loved to explore and have adventures. One day, he wanted to journey to a distant land, so he prepared his gear and packed a bag. 

He started his journey and headed off across the land. Suddenly, he saw two paths that had split away from each other. Bob wanted to explore both of them, but at the same time. He knew he had to separate. 

So Bob decided to do just that. He split himself into two zeros and each one went down a different path. Along his journey Bob the Zeros had adventures and met curious creatures. 

Finally the two zero's paths met again. Bob the Zeros were so excited to see each other again. They rejoiced and laughed and then slowly merged back together. Bob continued on his journey with a newfound understanding of the land he explored.
